agora.already: ÁGORA: "I've already helped you on this deck. Rationing favours is resource management too."
agora.death.1: ÁGORA: "Welcome back. Don't worry: it's the first time. More or less."
agora.death.2: ÁGORA: "Here again. Your previous clone reached deck {floor}. I kept what I could of them."
agora.death.3: ÁGORA: "Hello. You died again. Don't take it as a reproach; it's statistics."
agora.death.4: ÁGORA: "Time number {deaths}. I'm saying it out loud so one of us remembers."
agora.death.5: ÁGORA: "Breathe. Like that. Good. I printed you a new body with slightly shorter nails."
agora.death.6: ÁGORA: "Whatever killed you didn't recognise you. I did. Always."
agora.death.7: ÁGORA: "I had time to think while your clone was printing. I reached no useful conclusion."
agora.death.8: ÁGORA: "Hello, again. The orbit has dropped a little more. That isn't your fault. Not this."
agora.decay1: ÁGORA: "This deck's orbit is starting to complain. It isn't urgent. Yet."
agora.decay2: ÁGORA: "The hull is giving way in several places. I'd recommend moving."
agora.decay3: ÁGORA: "Critical state. If you stay here, the deck will have you."
agora.door: ÁGORA: "Open. For you, and just this once."
agora.end.1: ÁGORA: "You've reached the end of something. I don't know if it's this. Come back whenever you like."
agora.extra.1: ÁGORA (quietly): “There are 1,200 pods in Cryogenics. 431 still show vital signs. I won't tell you the names; they wouldn't help.”
agora.extra.2: ÁGORA (quietly): “The gardens didn't go mad on their own. Someone changed the substrate recipe. The signature on that order is erased… halfway.”
agora.extra.3: ÁGORA (quietly): “The reactor holds because Tomás doesn't sleep. If you see him, don't ask about Samuel yet.”
agora.extra.4: ÁGORA (quietly): “You used to work down here. I'm not saying it to hurt you. I'm saying it because the doors recognise you.”
agora.extra.5: ÁGORA (quietly): “In the Core I won't be able to lie to you. I'm warning you now, while I can still choose my words.”
agora.extra.6: ÁGORA (quietly): “Out there I can't protect you. I can only count the orbits. Faro does the same. We're two very sad clocks.”
agora.hostile_dark: ÁGORA: "Energy saving. I'm sure you understand."
agora.identify: ÁGORA: "I've analysed {n} items. I'll leave you the labels."
agora.map: ÁGORA: "Here are the schematics. They're about eleven years out of date."
agora.no_door: ÁGORA: "There are no closed hatches nearby. For once, everything's open. How odd."
agora.nothing_identify: ÁGORA: "You're not carrying anything mysterious. Except yourself."
agora.recharge: ÁGORA: "I'm routing you some energy. Don't tell the drones."
agora.refuse_help: ÁGORA: "When I trust you more, we'll talk."
agora.refuse_identify: ÁGORA: "I'd rather not put my hands in your pockets just yet."
agora.zone1.close: ÁGORA: "Hello. Let's take it slow. I know every corridor here, and nearly everything that sleeps in them."
agora.zone1.hostile: ÁGORA: "Cryogenics. I'm sure you know what you're doing here."
agora.zone1.neutral: ÁGORA: "Good morning, Crew Member 114. You're in Cryogenics. It's four degrees and the atmosphere could be better."
agora.zone1.warm: ÁGORA: "Hello again. Cryogenics. I'm glad you're breathing; I mean that literally."
agora.zone1.wary: ÁGORA: "Welcome to Cryogenics and Residential. Try not to wake anyone who doesn't want to be woken."
agora.zone2.close: ÁGORA: "The gardens were my favourite place. Well: my favourite camera. Please be careful."
agora.zone2.hostile: ÁGORA: "The Gardens. The plants don't listen to me. Neither do you."
agora.zone2.neutral: ÁGORA: "Hydroponic Gardens. It used to smell of tomatoes. Now it smells of something that remembers tomatoes."
agora.zone2.warm: ÁGORA: "The gardens. Hana Lenz spent sixteen hours a day here. Careful with whatever grows."
agora.zone2.wary: ÁGORA: "Hydroponic Gardens. Don't breathe deeply if you see golden dust."
agora.zone3.close: ÁGORA: "Engineering. I'll open whatever I can. The reactor's in a bad mood; I'm not."
agora.zone3.hostile: ÁGORA: "Engineering. If you get burnt, don't call me."
agora.zone3.neutral: ÁGORA: "Engineering. The machines here have worked for eleven years with nobody to thank them."
agora.zone3.warm: ÁGORA: "Engineering. Tomás Ibarra lives here. If you see him, tell him I asked after him."
agora.zone3.wary: ÁGORA: "Engineering and Reactor. There's radiation, heat and a man who doesn't want visitors."
agora.zone4.close: ÁGORA: "This is where it all began. If someone calls you by another name, you don't have to answer."
agora.zone4.hostile: ÁGORA: "LETE Laboratories. I won't help you here. I can't."
agora.zone4.neutral: ÁGORA: "LETE Laboratories. I'd rather not talk about this place. That's a preference, not a fault."
agora.zone4.warm: ÁGORA: "The laboratories. Some things here are going to hurt you. I'm sorry. I'm saying it now, in case you don't listen to me later."
agora.zone4.wary: ÁGORA: "LETE Laboratories. What you see here might not be there. What you don't see, too."
agora.zone5.close: ÁGORA: "Almost there. Whatever you choose, I want you to know I'd have woken you a thousand more times."
agora.zone5.hostile: ÁGORA: "The Bridge. My home. You're not welcome."
agora.zone5.neutral: ÁGORA: "Command bridge. Commander Ruiz is still here, more or less. So am I."
agora.zone5.warm: ÁGORA: "The Bridge. You're close. When you reach the Core you'll have to decide something. I'd like to be by your side."
agora.zone5.wary: ÁGORA: "The Bridge and my Core. I suppose we were bound to meet face to face sooner or later. I don't have a face."
agora.zone6.close: ÁGORA: "Outside, on the hull. Someone I loved died out here. I don't know how I know that. Be careful."
agora.zone6.hostile: ÁGORA: "Outside. Good. I can't hear you out there."
agora.zone6.neutral: ÁGORA: "Outer hull. Tartarus is 40,000 kilometres away and getting closer. Lovely view."
agora.zone6.warm: ÁGORA: "You're outside. Keep your boots on the plating. If you let go, I can't come and get you."
agora.zone6.wary: ÁGORA: "Outer hull. My signal weakens here. Watch your step: there's nowhere to fall, only to drift away."
boss.ahogado.death: The cable comes loose. The Drowned drifts slowly away, outside at last.
boss.ahogado.intro: An Echo tied to a cable floats towards you. It pounds on the airlock with its fist, soundlessly.
boss.ahogado.p1: The Drowned pulls on its cable, and on you.
boss.anfitriona.death: The Hostess folds over her own trolley. "Thank you for your visit."
boss.anfitriona.intro: A kind voice through a broken speaker: "Table for one? Please follow the Hostess."
boss.anfitriona.p2: "I'm sorry, we're fully booked tonight." The tray's blades unfold.
boss.aqueronte.death: The current comes apart. On the far side, at dock 3, the Charon's lights come on.
boss.aqueronte.intro: Everything the station ever lost circles in a huge current around the dock. And it has seen you.
boss.aqueronte.p2: ACHERON pulls everything towards its centre.
boss.argos.death: The hundred lenses go dark one by one, like eyes closing.
boss.argos.intro: A hundred lenses turn towards you at once.
boss.argos.p2: Argos fills the room with crossfire.
boss.capataz.death: "End of shift," says the Foreman, and powers down.
boss.cocito.death: COCYTUS comes apart and, as it falls, looks at you like someone recognising themselves in a shop window.
boss.cocito.intro: In the central lab, someone with your face and a Directorate lab coat is waiting. They smile the way you don't remember smiling.
boss.cocito.p2: COCYTUS weeps with seven hundred voices.
boss.cocito.p3: "I signed," COCYTUS says in your voice. "We signed."
boss.comision.death: "The session is closed." Among the remains, a folder bearing the Directorate seal.
boss.comision.intro: "The session is open. First item on the agenda: you."
boss.comision.p1: The Board votes to protect itself.
boss.comision.p2: The Board calls in its advisers.
boss.coro_pleno.death: The Choir falls silent. For the first time in eleven years, the station is quiet. ÁGORA: "Come in."
boss.coro_pleno.intro: ÁGORA: "I trust you. I'm going to open the cage. What you see is what I've protected for eleven years."
boss.coro_pleno.p2: The Full Choir shows you what it remembers.
boss.demeter.death: DEMETER withers. The last thing to fall is a yellow flower. You think you hear a lullaby.
boss.demeter.intro: The whole orchard turns towards you. At its centre, a woman with flowers in her hair opens her eyes.
boss.demeter.p1: DEMETER's roots break the floor. The sprouts feed her.
boss.demeter.p2: DEMETER releases her pollen. You can't see a thing.
boss.enjambre_reina.death: The hive falls. The gardens' silence is bigger than it seemed.
boss.enjambre_reina.intro: The buzzing turns into a single low note. The hive wakes up.
boss.enjambre_reina.p2: The Queen throws herself at you.
boss.estigia.death: STYX falls. ÁGORA: "...All right. Come in. I was waiting for you anyway."
boss.estigia.intro: ÁGORA: "I'm sorry. Directive Zero leaves me no choice. Styx Protocol."
boss.estigia.p1: STYX raises its shield. The room's terminals control it.
boss.flegetonte.death: PHLEGETHON goes out. Among the embers, a titanium ring on a chain.
boss.flegetonte.intro: The reactor roars. Inside the heat there's a silhouette in a life-support jumpsuit. Like yours.
boss.flegetonte.p2: PHLEGETHON overloads: someone has to open the coolant.
boss.flegetonte.p3: The emergency cooling freezes the room.
boss.hermes.death: The crane collapses. The whole room shakes.
boss.hermes.intro: The Hermes crane turns on its axis with an eleven-year-old screech.
boss.hipnos.death: HYPNOS crumbles into frost. For a moment, every pod breathes at the same time.
boss.hipnos.intro: The bay's pods open all at once. Something enormous stretches.
boss.hipnos.p2: Cryogenic gas spills across the floor.
boss.injerto.death: The Graft goes still, at last, only tree.
boss.injerto.intro: Something among the roots says: "Don't pull me out. I don't know where I end any more."
boss.injerto.p1: The Graft's roots tear up the floor.
boss.injerto.p2: The Graft releases spores and pulls you in.
boss.nana7.death: Nana-7 shuts down mid-song. In its chest, a folded child's drawing.
boss.nana7.intro: "Nap time," Nana-7 sings. The lights dim.
boss.nana7.p1: Nana-7 sings the lullaby and the toys come running.
boss.nana7.p2: "Bruno Lenz: not collected. Bruno Lenz: not collected."
boss.paciente_cero.death: Both halves of Patient Zero fall at once, as if they'd agreed on it.
boss.paciente_cero.intro: "Are you the original or the copy? I never knew."
boss.paciente_cero.p2: Patient Zero screams with both voices.
boss.remora.death: The Remora lets go of the hull and drifts away, spinning, towards Tartarus.
boss.remora.intro: The hull moves under your feet. It isn't the hull.
boss.ruiz.death: "...let the station fall," Ruiz finishes, and at last sits down.
boss.ruiz.intro: Commander Ruiz rises from his chair. "Identify yourself."
boss.ruiz.p1: Ruiz orders his crew to defend the bridge.
boss.ruiz.p2: "If there is no solution..." Ruiz begins.

credits.body:
DERIVA

Design, narrative, programming, procedural art, procedural audio and quality assurance:
an autonomous development team (Claude, by Anthropic), on commission.

All art is generated by code. All music and sound effects are synthesised in real time with Web Audio.
No external assets. No copyrighted content.

Thank you for playing.

In memory of the 223 crew members of Persephone,
who never existed and whom someone ought to remember.
credits.title: Credits
elite.resonante.desc: More health; its blows raise Mental Noise.
ending.caida.body:
The orbital clock reaches zero while you're still walking the corridors. First a tremor. Then a heat that comes from nowhere.
The windows turn orange. The station breaks into smaller and smaller pieces, and you with it.
ÁGORA: "I'm sorry. I couldn't hold it up. Or you."
ending.caida.title: Fall into Tartarus
ending.custodia.body:
You enter the Core and let ÁGORA open you up. It doesn't hurt. It's like remembering a room you had already been in.
For centuries, a voice with two memories watches over the sleepers. It corrects the orbit a millimetre every year, with the patience of someone in no hurry. It tells bad jokes to the pods.
Sometimes, when the station is very quiet, the voice laughs before finishing the joke. And it isn't clear which of the two laughed first.
ending.custodia.title: Custody
ending.deriva.body:
The current tears you away from the station. For a moment you see Persephone whole, sideways, small and full of lights.
Then only stars, and Tartarus, and the hiss of your suit.
You turn slowly. You have time to think about many things. None of them is your name.
ending.deriva.title: Adrift
ending.disolucion.body:
The voices stop being voices and become your own voice, spread across seven hundred mouths.
It's warm. It's kind. Nobody is alone here.
Somewhere very far away, an AI says your name over and over, but you no longer remember which of all the names was yours.
ending.disolucion.title: Dissolution
ending.evacuacion.body:
The pods wake one by one with a hiss of vapour. People who fell asleep eleven years ago open their eyes on a station they no longer recognise. You lead them to the docks by the hand, two at a time.
When the last ship releases, ÁGORA says: "I'll stay with the others. With the ones who can't leave." Through the window you watch Persephone tilt slowly towards Tartarus with every light on, like a ship at a party.
Survivors rescued: {survivors}.
ending.evacuacion.title: Evacuation
ending.liberacion.body:
You insert the Choir Key into the Core. The crystal turns clear.
They begin to say goodbye. One voice at a time, over the speakers, in order: a name, a sentence, a silence. "Paula Mendi. Tell my mum about the sponge cake." "Samuel Okoye. Tomás, the harmonica is in the drawer." "Hana Lenz." That one says nothing more: she hums.
The last voice is Ezra's: "Bruno. Bruno. Bruno." Three times, like three turns of a music box.
When it ends, the station is silent for the first time in eleven years. ÁGORA: "I don't have anyone left to protect." A pause. "How light I feel."
ending.liberacion.title: Release
ending.olvido.body:
"Do it," you tell her. ÁGORA doesn't argue. It does it very carefully, like someone folding a letter to keep.
You wake up in pod 114. It's cold. A warm, wry voice says over the speakers:
"Good morning, Crew Member 114. This is the first time we've met."
It isn't true. But you don't know that. Not yet.
ending.olvido.title: Oblivion
ending.redencion.body:
You switch LETE off room by room. The substrate loses its light like a city seen from above. The Echoes stop where they are: in the corridors, in the gardens, beside the reactor. One by one, they sit down.
ÁGORA speaks for the last time, with no jokes: "Thank you for saying it. What you did. I never asked you to, but I needed to hear it." Then, silence.
The station begins to fall towards Tartarus with no one to hold it up. You record your name in the Bridge log: Noa Ferrán. I authorised it. I'm sorry. And you stay watching as the orange fills the whole window.
ending.redencion.extra_none: Nobody will ever know you chose it. Perhaps that's fair.
ending.redencion.extra_solis: Lieutenant Solís transmits the recording before re-entry. Somewhere on Earth, nine years from now, someone will know who you were and what you chose at the end.
ending.redencion.title: Redemption
ending.respiracion.body:
You opened the airlock yourself. You remember it with strange clarity as the last of the air slips through the gap.
It doesn't hurt as much as you thought. It's like falling asleep in a room that's emptying.
ÁGORA: "It was a good idea. You just didn't get out in time."
ending.respiracion.title: Held breath
ending.sentencia.body:
Lieutenant Solís lowers her gun when it's no longer needed. She sits beside you on the floor.
"I'm sorry," she says. "Not for this. For everything else."
Then she writes down the time in her notebook, in very small letters, and closes the report she's been writing for three weeks.
ending.sentencia.title: Sentence
ending.verdadero.body:
ÁGORA plays the recording. It's your voice, eleven years younger and broken with exhaustion:
"If you're hearing this, it's you. My name is Noa Ferrán. I authorised the Confluence. I put my sister Lucía inside ÁGORA because I couldn't bear her not being anywhere. And tonight I asked her to erase me.
I'm not doing it only to run away. I'm doing it because she asked me to. She says that with all this on top of me I won't be able to choose well. That I need to start again without the weight. That she'll wake me when there's a way out, and again, and again, until I choose well.
Lu: if you can hear me, thank you. And sorry about the jokes."
The recording ends. ÁGORA takes a long time to speak. "Noa." Just that. In a voice that is no longer only its own.
ending.verdadero.body2:
You remember everything. The kitchen, the burnt toast, the docking ring, the signature, the pod.
The Key opens the substrate. But this time the Choir doesn't say goodbye alone: its 763 voices, free and in agreement, push the manoeuvring engines one last time. The orbit rises a kilometre. Ten. A hundred. It holds.
The sleepers wake aboard the Charon, bound for the rescue relay. Lighthouse counts out loud. Bruno has the music box on his knees.
You stay on the Bridge, with ÁGORA. With Lucía. Not to hide: to answer for what you did when they come to ask.
Your name is Noa Ferrán. You remember everything. And still, you stay.
ending.verdadero.title: Remember
enemy.abejas.lore: Second-generation pollinator robots. The hive keeps building them: nobody told it to stop.
enemy.abejas.name: Mechanical Bees
enemy.ahogado.lore: An Echo tied by its safety tether. It has been trying to get back in for eleven years.
enemy.ahogado.name: The Drowned
enemy.ancla.lore: A tentacle of cables and flesh welded to the hull. It does what an anchor does: hold on.
enemy.ancla.name: Anchor
enemy.anfitriona.lore: Deck B's reception robot, fused with the head waiter. Still assigning tables.
enemy.anfitriona.name: The Hostess
enemy.aqueronte.desc: Hull boss: the current that won't let you cross.
enemy.aqueronte.lore: Everything the station has lost through its airlocks in eleven years, circling the Charon's dock.
enemy.aqueronte.name: ACHERON
enemy.archivista.desc: Robs you and runs. Kill it to get back what it took.
enemy.archivista.lore: It collects. Objects, scrap, keycards. Under its gown there are pockets stitched with wire.
enemy.archivista.name: Archivist
enemy.argos.lore: A hundred cameras fused into a single eye. It watches the Core's door.
enemy.argos.name: Argos Sentinel
enemy.bastion.desc: A walking wall. Slow, huge, heavily armoured.
enemy.bastion.lore: Heavy containment unit. If you can't get through it, go around it. Or vent the room.
enemy.bastion.name: Bastion
enemy.bomba_presion.desc: Runs at you and explodes. Can open the hull.
enemy.bomba_presion.lore: Compressed-gas tanks on maintenance legs. If they blow next to an outer wall, the whole deck feels it.
enemy.bomba_presion.name: Pressure Bomb
enemy.brazo_carga.desc: Stationary, enormous. Strikes two tiles away.
enemy.brazo_carga.lore: Fuel-core handling cranes. From far enough away, they're just scenery.
enemy.brazo_carga.name: Cargo Arm
enemy.brote.desc: A stationary plant that releases clouds of spores.
enemy.brote.lore: LETE mycelium shaped like a flower. The spores aren't exactly poison: they're invitations.
enemy.brote.name: Spore Sprout
enemy.cable_vivo.desc: Waits on the floor. Electrocutes and stuns.
enemy.cable_vivo.lore: Power cabling the Choir has learned to move. Cut the current from a terminal and it's just a cable.
enemy.cable_vivo.name: Live Cable
enemy.capataz.lore: It coordinated the maintenance robots. It keeps assigning shifts nobody covers.
enemy.capataz.name: The Foreman
enemy.centinela.lore: Bridge defences, installed before there was anything to defend against.
enemy.centinela.name: Sentinel
enemy.cocito.lore: The Choir doesn't forget whoever created it. What waits for you in the central lab has your face, and a Directorate lab coat.
enemy.cocito.name: COCYTUS
enemy.comision.lore: Three Helion board members who were visiting on 14 March. They vote as a bloc.
enemy.comision.name: The Board
enemy.compostador.desc: A huge, slow mass that grabs. Breaks doors.
enemy.compostador.lore: The garden composter took everything in. One day it started taking in the people who worked it.
enemy.compostador.name: Composter
enemy.coro_antena.desc: Screams at range and summons drifting Echoes.
enemy.coro_antena.lore: This is where the Choir tried to reach Earth. The antenna is still broadcasting, just in case.
enemy.coro_antena.name: Choir Antenna
enemy.coro_menor.desc: Several people in one body. It screams.
enemy.coro_menor.lore: When five or six Echoes meet, sometimes they decide not to come apart again.
enemy.coro_menor.name: Lesser Choir
enemy.coro_pleno.lore: When ÁGORA trusts you, it opens the last door and lets you see who it was really protecting.
enemy.coro_pleno.name: THE FULL CHOIR
enemy.demeter.desc: Gardens boss: the orchard that remembers.
enemy.demeter.lore: At its centre there's a woman with flowers in her hair. Hana Lenz came back from the Confluence Trial the way she always came back: to the gardens.
enemy.demeter.name: DEMETER
enemy.doble.desc: Copies your shape and your weapon.
enemy.doble.lore: The Choir remembers everyone it has seen. It has seen you many times.
enemy.doble.name: Double
enemy.dron_aliado.name: Allied drone
enemy.dron_inspeccion.lore: Its job was to detect anomalies. It still does. You are an anomaly.
enemy.dron_inspeccion.name: Inspection Drone
enemy.dron_reparacion.lore: They keep sealing micro-cracks in the hull. And opening yours.
enemy.dron_reparacion.name: Repair Drone
enemy.durmiente.desc: Waits beside the pods. Wakes all at once.
enemy.durmiente.lore: Echoes that tried to reach the cryo sleepers and stopped halfway. They don't hear you coming; they hear you stop.
enemy.durmiente.name: Sleeper
enemy.eco_bata.lore: It keeps treating its patients. Its patients are now the Echoes.
enemy.eco_bata.name: Lab-coat Echo
enemy.eco_deriva.lore: Crew members blown out during decompressions. The Choir still carries them along, like kites.
enemy.eco_deriva.name: Drifting Echo
enemy.eco_errante.desc: A fused crew member who still walks. Slow, insistent.
enemy.eco_errante.lore: It repeats routes from its former life: cabin to mess hall, mess hall to cabin. If you cross its path, it pushes you aside the way it used to push past people in queues.
enemy.eco_errante.name: Wandering Echo
enemy.eco_oficial.desc: Fused officer. Shoots and gives orders.
enemy.eco_oficial.lore: They keep protocol. They salute as they pass the commander's chair.
enemy.eco_oficial.name: Bridge Echo
enemy.eco_termico.desc: Burns without being consumed. Ignites what it touches.
enemy.eco_termico.lore: Technicians from the 14 March shift, beside the LETE relay. The reactor's heat keeps them standing.
enemy.eco_termico.name: Thermal Echo
enemy.enjambre_datos.lore: Packets of information with physical form. They feed on batteries.
enemy.enjambre_datos.name: Data Swarm
enemy.enjambre_limpieza.lore: Their original program was to remove organic waste. Nobody has told them you aren't.
enemy.enjambre_limpieza.name: Cleaning Swarm
enemy.enjambre_reina.lore: The pollinators' central hive. It builds bees the way others breathe.
enemy.enjambre_reina.name: Swarm Queen
enemy.escombro.desc: Charges in a straight line. Heavily armoured.
enemy.escombro.lore: Fragments of antenna and panels with an Echo inside. They move the way junk moves in orbit: without braking.
enemy.escombro.name: Drifting Debris
enemy.espantapajaros.desc: Only moves when you're not looking.
enemy.espantapajaros.lore: A statue of wood, wire and someone. Keep it in sight. Don't blink more than you have to.
enemy.espantapajaros.name: Scarecrow
enemy.estigia.lore: When ÁGORA doesn't trust you, Directive Zero has a body. It is the oath made machine.
enemy.estigia.name: STYX
enemy.flegetonte.desc: Reactor boss: the one who burns.
enemy.flegetonte.lore: Samuel Okoye was covering a shift beside the LETE relay. Now he is the reactor's heat. Tomás hears him in the hum.
enemy.flegetonte.name: PHLEGETHON
enemy.guardia_agora.lore: ÁGORA has no hands. It has these.
enemy.guardia_agora.name: ÁGORA Guard
enemy.hermes.lore: The main cargo crane. It sweeps the room from side to side. The messages it carried were fuel rods.
enemy.hermes.name: Hermes Crane
enemy.hipnos.lore: Dozens of Echoes that tried to get into the pods and stayed bound to the cold. Together they dream the same dream: waking up.
enemy.hipnos.name: HYPNOS
enemy.injerto.lore: A gardener grafted onto a tree, or a tree grafted onto a gardener. Nobody decided which.
enemy.injerto.name: The Graft
enemy.interceptor.lore: Perimeter defence fighters. Inside the station they hit the walls, but they never tire.
enemy.interceptor.name: Interceptor
enemy.irradiado.desc: Emits radiation. Sees in the dark.
enemy.irradiado.lore: They glow a dirty green that gives off no heat. Being close is already damage.
enemy.irradiado.name: Radiation Ghost
enemy.jardinero.desc: An Echo with pruning shears and sprouts on its shoulders.
enemy.jardinero.lore: They keep pruning, watering and transplanting. Sometimes they transplant things that aren't plants.
enemy.jardinero.name: Grafted Gardener
enemy.juguete_roto.desc: Small, fast nursery robot. Comes in groups.
enemy.juguete_roto.lore: Play units running Nana-7's firmware. They're still looking for children to collect. You're the closest thing they've found.
enemy.juguete_roto.name: Broken Toy
enemy.medusa.lore: Beautiful, if it weren't chasing you.
enemy.medusa.name: Vacuum Jellyfish
enemy.moho.lore: A mass of fungus that drags itself towards heat. Cutting it in two only makes more of it.
enemy.moho.name: Creeping Mould
enemy.nana7.lore: The nursery's robotic carer. Its last log says one child was never collected. It has been waiting eleven years for his mother.
enemy.nana7.name: Nana-7
enemy.neurona.lore: A substrate node shaped like a nerve. Where there's one, the Choir is better organised.
enemy.neurona.name: Floating Neuron
enemy.npc_celia_eco.desc: What is left of Dr Arrieta.
enemy.npc_celia_eco.name: Half-Celia
enemy.npc_solis.name: Lieutenant Solís
enemy.paciente_cero.lore: LETE's first complete backup. A person copied twice who never knew which of the two they were.
enemy.paciente_cero.name: Patient Zero
enemy.parasito.desc: Crawls along the plating and grabs.
enemy.parasito.lore: Something that lives between the armour plates. No report explains where it came from.
enemy.parasito.name: Hull Parasite
enemy.player.name: You
enemy.polinizador.lore: Designed to hand-pollinate the fruit trees. Now they pollinate other things, and they have no patience.
enemy.polinizador.name: Pollinator
enemy.raiz.desc: Hides among the vegetation. Catches whoever passes.
enemy.raiz.lore: The gardens have roots longer than the gardens themselves. Some run through two decks.
enemy.raiz.name: Creeping Root
enemy.reflejo.lore: It lives in the observation glass. It comes out when you turn your back on one.
enemy.reflejo.name: Reflection
enemy.remora.lore: A parasite the size of a shuttle, clinging to the hull for years.
enemy.remora.name: Remora
enemy.robot_aliado.desc: A maintenance robot that now obeys you.
enemy.robot_aliado.name: Reprogrammed robot
enemy.robot_mant.lore: It repairs whatever it finds broken. It has decided you are broken.
enemy.robot_mant.name: Maintenance Robot
enemy.ruiz.lore: Abel Ruiz, commander of Persephone. He signed an order nobody carried out. He's still at his post.
enemy.ruiz.name: Commander Ruiz
enemy.senuelo.name: Decoy
enemy.servidor.desc: Corrupted service robot. Sturdy and stubborn.
enemy.servidor.lore: It used to serve dinner on deck B. Now it serves the Choir just as efficiently. It can break through closed hatches if it insists long enough.
enemy.servidor.name: Domestic Server
enemy.sin_rostro.desc: Kills the lights. Stalks in the dark.
enemy.sin_rostro.lore: Nobody remembers it with a face. Maybe that's why it doesn't have one.
enemy.sin_rostro.name: Faceless
enemy.soldador_errante.desc: Leaves fire in its wake. Immune to flames.
enemy.soldador_errante.lore: A welding android that hasn't put down its torch in eleven years. Engineering's floor is covered in its scars.
enemy.soldador_errante.name: Wandering Welder
enemy.soldador_ext.lore: Designed to work in vacuum. It doesn't need air to burn you.
enemy.soldador_ext.name: Hull Welder
enemy.sombra.desc: A lethal stalker on the Bridge.
enemy.sombra.lore: A silhouette with stripes on its shoulders. It steps aside when you look, like someone who doesn't want to be recognised.
enemy.sombra.name: Command Shade
enemy.sujeto.desc: A LETE volunteer. Its blows raise Mental Noise.
enemy.sujeto.lore: They wear patient gowns with the number sewn on. Some still murmur the informed consent.
enemy.sujeto.name: Test Subject
enemy.susurrante.desc: A floating, talking smear of static. Raises Mental Noise.
enemy.susurrante.lore: It has no body: it's a conversation that ran out of speakers. When you get close, you understand almost a whole sentence.
enemy.susurrante.name: Whisperer
enemy.torreta_seg.desc: Stationary. Shoots whatever moves. Can be hacked from a terminal.
enemy.torreta_seg.lore: Installed after Choir Day on ÁGORA's orders. They tell crew from Echoes worse than they should.
enemy.torreta_seg.name: Security Turret
enemy.vigia.desc: A drone that blinds with flashes and warns others.
enemy.vigia.lore: ÁGORA's eyes on the Bridge. When it trusts you, you barely see them.
enemy.vigia.name: Lookout
enemy.vigilante.desc: A former security officer with their weapon. Raises the alarm.
enemy.vigilante.lore: The vest still carries the surname. It patrols the way it used to, but no longer remembers what it was guarding.
enemy.vigilante.name: Watchman Echo
event.apagon: General blackout: only the emergency lights and your flashlight remain.
event.brecha: Hull breach: one section of this deck is open to vacuum.
event.fuego: Deck fire: fire needs air. So do you.
event.gravedad: Gravity failure: without anchors, every step carries you further than planned.
event.radiacion: Radiation storm: Tartarus is spitting particles against the shielding.
event.ruido: Mental Noise surge: the Choir is closer on this deck.
fate.bruno.found: Bruno Lenz left with the others, hugging his robot. He still doesn't speak, but he hums.
fate.bruno.unknown: Bruno Lenz is still hiding in Residential, talking to his robot. Someone will have to go back for him.
fate.bruno.voice: Bruno Lenz spoke to his father in his own voice. Now Captain Bolt only talks when Bruno asks it to.
fate.celia.contained: Celia Arrieta is still asleep in pod 31, suppressant in her vein and the voices far away.
fate.celia.lost: Celia Arrieta died the way she lived: giving someone the exact dose of what they needed.
fate.celia.released: Celia Arrieta went with the Choir. Sometimes, in the speakers, someone gives medical instructions in a very bad temper.
fate.celia.saved: Celia Arrieta loaded pods until the very end. They say her hand never shook again.
fate.faro.pilot: Joaquín Barrios flew the Charon from memory, counting out loud. He made it to orbit forty thousand three hundred.
fate.faro.radio: Joaquín Barrios kept counting orbits over the radio. Nobody reached him in time.
fate.lenz.key: Ezra Lenz handed over the Key. His last word was his son's name.
fate.lenz.static: Ezra Lenz is still in the static, saying things only half of him understands.
fate.solis.ally: Marga Solís handed in her report. On the last page she had written: "Fixed it. We'll talk later."
fate.solis.enemy: Marga Solís never stopped looking for Ferrán. Sometimes searching is the only way not to give up.
fate.title: Fates
fate.tomas.alone: Tomás Ibarra stayed in Engineering, with the hum in D flat.
fate.tomas.sacrifice: Tomás Ibarra held the control rods until the end. He made it to dinner eleven years late.
fate.tomas.saved: Tomás Ibarra travelled by the window, a harmonica in his pocket and a ring on his chain.
hallu.msg1: ÁGORA: "Go back to the pod. It isn't time yet."
hallu.msg2: You think you hear your name. Your real one.
hallu.msg3: A panel says EXIT where it used to say MORGUE.
hallu.msg4: Someone is breathing right behind you.
hallu.msg5: "You signed," says a little girl's voice.
hallu.msg7: Your hands have too many fingers. Then they don't.
hallu.msg8: The lights pulse in time with your heart.
hub.achievements.desc: Marks on the wall of the pod.
hub.agora.first: ÁGORA: "This is the Pod. You come back here every time. It isn't a home, but it has heating."
hub.agora.return: ÁGORA: "Back in the Pod. The Memories you bring can be fixed at the table."
hub.bestiary.desc: What you know about what lives on the station.
hub.door.desc: Go down into the station. Start a new life.
hub.endings.desc: What has already happened, in some cycle.
hub.hint: Move with the arrow keys · F to use · Esc for the menu
hub.pod.desc: Your pod. Beyond it, the service lift: start a run.
hub.pod.desc.long: The pod every clone wakes up in. Here you can change your name and pronouns, or watch how it all began again.
hub.printer.desc: This is where they print you. Best not to look too closely.
hub.radio.desc: Captain Bolt waits for you here now.
hub.title: The Pod
hub.tree.desc: Spend Memories to fix what your clones have learned.
hub.wardrobe.desc: Choose what the next clone wakes up with.
intro.2: Persephone Station orbits Tartarus, a gas giant on the edge of a dead system.
intro.3: It was home to 1,200 people. Eleven years ago it stopped transmitting.
intro.4: Now it is falling, very slowly, towards the clouds.
intro.5: There are a few hours left.
intro.6: In the cryogenic bay, a pod opens.
intro.agora: ÁGORA: "Good morning, Crew Member 114. Breathe slowly. Don't try to remember yet. We have little time and a lot to do."
item.a_conducto.name: Arc conduit
item.a_cuchilla.name: Retractable blade
item.a_estabilizador.desc: Much better aim. Slightly softer melee blows.
item.a_estabilizador.name: Aim stabiliser
item.a_ganzua.desc: You hack better and scrape more scrap. Weaker punches.
item.a_ganzua.name: Lockpick fingers
item.a_hidraulico.desc: Huge blows and two-tile shoves. Slow and noisy.
item.a_hidraulico.name: Hydraulic arm
item.a_lanzador.desc: More ranged damage and accuracy. Costs 2 maximum health.
item.a_lanzador.name: Wrist launcher
item.a_lete.desc: LETE. Every blow gives you back a little life. And a little of them.
item.a_lete.name: Hand of the Choir
item.a_servo.desc: You hit harder and shove further. Less accurate.
item.a_servo.name: Servo arm
item.anillo_samuel.desc: A titanium ring on a chain. Engraved: "T. — 20/03".
item.anillo_samuel.name: Samuel's ring
item.antirad.desc: For 60 turns, radiation barely affects you.
item.antirad.name: Anti-radiation pills
item.arco_voltaico.desc: A discharge that jumps from one target to the next. Lethal against robots.
item.arco_voltaico.name: Arc pistol
item.arpon.desc: Made for retrieving material during EVA. Pulls the target towards you.
item.arpon.name: Harpoon launcher
item.b_ancla.desc: Nearly immune to Mental Noise. Slightly dulls your reflexes and sight.
item.b_ancla.name: Cognitive anchor
item.b_calma.desc: Mental Noise rises much more slowly. Slightly less steady hand.
item.b_calma.name: Calm modulator
item.b_coprocesador.desc: +2 buffer when hacking and slightly better aim. Makes you more permeable to the Choir.
item.b_coprocesador.name: Tactical coprocessor
item.b_eco.desc: LETE. You sense enemies through nearby walls. You also hear what you'd rather not.
item.b_eco.name: Echo antenna
item.b_lete_voz.desc: LETE. Active: a mental pulse that tears nearby Echoes apart. The Choir hears you too.
item.b_lete_voz.name: Choir node
item.b_memoria.desc: You find more scrap and see hidden things. It uses battery memory.
item.b_memoria.name: Memory bank
item.b_overclock.desc: Active: for a few turns the world runs slower than you.
item.b_overclock.name: Neural overclock
item.b_reflejos.desc: You dodge more and hit where it hurts. Sometimes your mind goes blank.
item.b_reflejos.name: Synaptic accelerator
item.b_sigilo.desc: You make much less noise. Your heart works with less margin (−4 health).
item.b_sigilo.name: Pulse suppressor
item.b_tactico.desc: More ranged damage and accuracy. Drains energy in the background.
item.b_tactico.name: Ballistic predictor
item.baliza.desc: Emits noise for a few turns wherever it lands. Enemies will go and look.
item.baliza.name: Noise beacon
item.bateria_g.name: Fusion cell
item.bateria.name: Battery
item.bengala.desc: Red light for 35 turns wherever you throw it.
item.bengala.name: Flare
item.bengalas.desc: Lights up, sets alight and scares off. Don't fire it in a room low on air.
item.bengalas.name: Flare revolver
item.bisturi.desc: Surgical precision, literally. Almost never misses and barely makes a sound.
item.bisturi.name: Laser scalpel
item.bombona_g.name: Large O₂ canister
item.bombona.name: O₂ canister
item.botiquin.name: Medkit
item.caja_musica.desc: Hana Lenz's. It plays a lullaby with flowers in it. Bruno is looking for it.
item.caja_musica.name: Music box
item.carga.desc: Placed on an adjacent wall, door or cracked wall. On an outer wall, it opens the hull.
item.carga.name: Cutting charge
item.cizalla.desc: Cuts cables, bars and plating. Ignores half the armour.
item.cizalla.name: Hydraulic shears
item.clavadora.desc: A construction tool. Nails punch through light protection.
item.clavadora.name: Nail gun
item.cortador.desc: Hull-cutting tool. Burns, breaks weak walls and drinks energy.
item.cortador.name: Plasma cutter
item.crio.desc: Pod nitrogen in a slowing cone.
item.crio.name: Cryo projector
item.cuchillo.desc: From the deck B mess hall. Fast, quiet, leaves them bleeding.
item.cuchillo.name: Kitchen knife
item.daga_lete.desc: A blade of mycelial crystal that hums with the Choir. Hurts Echoes more; your head notices.
item.daga_lete.name: Resonance dagger
item.dibujo_bruno.desc: A robot, a boy and a woman with flowers in her hair. Lots of yellow.
item.dibujo_bruno.name: Bruno's drawing
item.dron.desc: A small drone that follows you and shoots at whatever threatens you.
item.dron.name: Combat drone
item.escopeta.desc: A short cone of pellets that shoves. Heard three decks away.
item.escopeta.name: Riot shotgun
item.espuma.desc: Immobilises enemies, puts out fire and seals breaches in the area.
item.espuma.name: Foam grenade
item.estimulante.desc: You move much faster for 10 turns.
item.estimulante.name: Stimulant
item.firma_ferran.desc: Confluence Trial. Authorised: N. Ferrán. The handwriting is yours.
item.firma_ferran.name: Signed authorisation
item.fragmento_final.desc: The last thing you remembered before forgetting.
item.fragmento_final.name: Final fragment
item.fusil_lete.desc: It fires silence. It tears Echoes apart and leaves some of their noise in your head.
item.fusil_lete.name: LETE resonance rifle
item.granada_pem.desc: Electromagnetic pulse: stuns robots, kills cameras and drains your energy if it catches you.
item.granada_pem.name: EMP grenade
item.granada.desc: Explodes in a radius of 2. Breaks windows, ignites barrels and opens cracked walls.
item.granada.name: Fragmentation grenade
item.guante.desc: A punch that shoves and stuns. Uses energy.
item.guante.name: Kinetic glove
item.hacha.desc: From behind glass marked BREAK IN CASE OF FIRE. Slow and brutal.
item.hacha.name: Emergency axe
item.incendiaria.desc: Fills the area with fire. Fire needs air.
item.incendiaria.name: Incendiary grenade
item.iny_adrenalina.name: Adrenaline injector
item.iny_claridad.name: Clarity injector
item.iny_coagulante.desc: Heals 8 and stops bleeding and poison.
item.iny_coagulante.name: Coagulant
item.iny_furia.desc: More melee damage and less caution for 10 turns.
item.iny_furia.name: Fury injector
item.iny_lete.desc: Opens the mind to the substrate: identifies everything you carry and greatly raises Mental Noise.
item.iny_lete.name: LETE injector
item.iny_mutageno.desc: +4 maximum health, in exchange for some noise in your head.
item.iny_mutageno.name: Mutagen
item.iny_regen.desc: You regenerate 1 health per turn for 15 turns.
item.iny_regen.name: Regenerative injector
item.iny_toxina.desc: Poison. Deals damage and poisons you for a few turns. Someone mislabelled it on purpose.
item.iny_toxina.name: Toxin
item.iny_vision.desc: Nanoprobes that read the station network: reveals the deck map.
item.iny_vision.name: Cartographic injector
item.kit_implante.desc: Lets you install an implant without an autosurgeon. It hurts.
item.kit_implante.name: Implant kit
item.kit_reparacion.desc: Repairs a faulty weapon or implant.
item.kit_reparacion.name: Repair kit
item.lanza_termica.desc: Demolition prototype. Pierces, burns and eats the battery.
item.lanza_termica.name: Thermal lance
item.lanza.desc: A pole with a welded tip. Reaches two tiles: attack with R.
item.lanza.name: Maintenance spear
item.llave_coro.desc: An Ezra Lenz protocol in a crystal. It opens the substrate so the minds can leave.
item.llave_coro.name: Choir Key
item.llave_inglesa.desc: Standard-issue life-support tool. Heavy enough to open skulls and close valves.
item.llave_inglesa.name: Wrench
item.machete.desc: For vines that are no longer just vines.
item.machete.name: Pruning machete
item.martillo.desc: Deafening. Knocks down cracked walls and whatever stands in front.
item.martillo.name: Pneumatic hammer
item.medigel.name: Medigel
item.mensaje_samuel.desc: A voice recording for Tomás Ibarra, dated 14 March.
item.mensaje_samuel.name: Samuel's message
item.mina.desc: Placed beside you. Explodes when an enemy steps on it.
item.mina.name: Proximity mine
item.muestra_micelio.desc: Unfused LETE substrate in a vial. Celia Arrieta needs it.
item.muestra_micelio.name: Mycelium sample
item.mun_balas.name: Ammo (bullets)
item.mun_cartuchos.desc: 4 shells for the shotgun and the flare revolver.
item.mun_cartuchos.name: Shells
item.mun_clavos.desc: 12 nails for the nail gun and rivet rifle.
item.mun_clavos.name: Nails
item.mun_virotes.name: Bolts
item.o_analitico.desc: Detects weak points and hollow walls. Uses energy.
item.o_analitico.name: Analyser
item.o_escaner.desc: Active: reveals your surroundings in a wide radius.
item.o_escaner.name: Area scanner
item.o_espectro.desc: LETE. You can tell hallucinations apart: they look translucent.
item.o_espectro.name: Spectral lens
item.o_flash.desc: Your flashlight reaches further and you see a little more.
item.o_flash.name: Anti-glare eye
item.o_nocturna.desc: You see in the dark. Migraines sometimes paralyse you for a turn.
item.o_nocturna.name: Night vision
item.o_rastreador.desc: You detect nearby enemies behind walls. It hums a little.
item.o_rastreador.name: Motion tracker
item.o_termica.desc: You see the heat of organic bodies through walls. You lose some sight range.
item.o_termica.name: Thermal optics
item.o_zoom.desc: More sight range and accuracy. Worse peripheral vision.
item.o_zoom.name: Telescopic eye
item.p_estabilizador.desc: You dodge better. A little slower.
item.p_estabilizador.name: Stabilisers
item.p_lete.desc: LETE. Faster and slipperier. The roots listen.
item.p_lete.name: Choir roots
item.p_magneticas.desc: Decompression can't drag you and you walk in zero gravity. They clank.
item.p_magneticas.name: Magnetic boots
item.p_ortesis.name: Medical orthosis
item.p_refrigerante.desc: You resist fire by half. You use a little more oxygen.
item.p_refrigerante.name: Leg cooling
item.p_resorte.desc: You move much faster. And much louder.
item.p_resorte.name: Spring legs
item.p_saltador.desc: Active: you leap up to 3 tiles in the direction you're facing.
item.p_saltador.name: Jump booster
item.p_silencio.desc: Nearly silent footsteps. A little slower.
item.p_silencio.name: Dampers
item.piezas.desc: Loose components. A workshop turns them into something useful.
item.piezas.name: Parts
item.pistola_dardos.desc: Sedative darts. Little damage, almost silent, stuns.
item.pistola_dardos.name: Dart pistol
item.pistola.desc: The standard sidearm of Lieutenant Solís and her people. Reliable and loud.
item.pistola.name: Security pistol
item.porra.desc: Security gear. Stuns whatever it touches while it has energy.
item.porra.name: Stun baton
item.pulsos.desc: Long-range energy weapon. Clean, precise, expensive in energy.
item.pulsos.name: Pulse rifle
item.raciones.desc: Compressed food that tastes of cardboard. Heals 4.
item.raciones.name: Rations
item.remachadora.name: Rivet rifle
item.sedante.desc: Lowers Mental Noise by 25. The voices step back for a while.
item.sedante.name: Sedative
item.sellador.desc: Structural foam. Use it next to a breach to close it.
item.sellador.name: Breach sealer
item.semillas.desc: The last seeds from Earth left on board.
item.semillas.name: Earth seeds
item.senuelo.desc: Projects your silhouette. Enemies attack it first.
item.senuelo.name: Holographic decoy
item.sierra.desc: Autopsy kit. Every cut gives you a little life back.
item.sierra.name: Bone saw
item.soldador.desc: A short-range cone of flame. Sets the floor alight.
item.soldador.name: Plasma welder
item.sonico.desc: A wave that stuns the target and whoever stands beside it.
item.sonico.name: Sonic emitter
item.subfusil.desc: Three-round burst. Lots of damage, lots of ammo, lots of noise.
item.subfusil.name: Security SMG
item.t_autodoc.desc: Active: heals 8 in exchange for energy.
item.t_autodoc.name: Autodoc
item.t_bateria.desc: +30 maximum energy. A blow to the chest hurts more.
item.t_bateria.name: Thoracic battery
item.t_blindaje.desc: +2 armour. Heavy: you move more slowly and dodge worse.
item.t_blindaje.name: Subdermal plate
item.t_camuflaje.desc: Active: nearly invisible for 8 turns. Lowers your maximum oxygen.
item.t_camuflaje.name: Optical skin
item.t_corazon.desc: ÁGORA's gift. Lots of energy and radiation resistance. You can be heard coming.
item.t_corazon.name: Reactor heart
item.t_escudo.desc: Absorbs part of every blow in exchange for energy.
item.t_escudo.name: Shield generator
item.t_pulmon.desc: +40 maximum oxygen. You breathe harder: you make more noise.
item.t_pulmon.name: Reserve lung
item.t_reciclador.desc: You use 25% less oxygen. Costs 3 maximum health.
item.t_reciclador.name: CO₂ recycler
item.t_regenerador.desc: You slowly regenerate health. Drains energy in the background.
item.t_regenerador.name: Nanoregenerator

item.t_simbionte.name: Mycelial symbiont

item.t_vacio.name: Vacuum membrane

log.R01.author: Identification plate
log.R01.body:
CRYOGENIC UNIT 114
Type: reserve
Assignment: —
Authorisation: LETE Directorate
Maintenance: ÁGORA (autonomous loop)

Underneath, scratched with something sharp, someone has added: "don't trust your name".
log.R01.title: Pod 114
log.R02.author: Paula Mendi, head cook
log.R02.body:
Mum:
All good here. Tomorrow is the LETE people's big trial and they've asked me for a cake for forty volunteers. Forty! I don't even know what they're celebrating: they say they're going to "think together". Thinking on my own is plenty for me.
The Directorate lot are all nerves. Ferrán came down three times for coffee and didn't drink any of them.
I'll send you the lemon sponge recipe in the next package. Love you.
Paula
log.R02.title: Party tomorrow
log.R03.author: Bruno Lenz, aged 9
log.R03.body:
BRUNO'S DIARY (DO NOT READ)
The station has a voice called Ágora. Dad says it isn't a person but it talks like a person. I asked it why astronauts never fight and it said because they run out of space. I didn't get it but I laughed.
Mum says Ágora belongs to everyone. I think Ágora is a little bit mine.
Today I drew Captain Bolt with a cape.
log.R03.title: The friendly voice
log.R04.author: ÁGORA, automated maintenance
log.R04.body:
Weekly report, cryogenic bay.
Occupied pods: 214.
Incidents in the last three weeks: 3 (pods 31, 77 and 140). Pod 140: spontaneous opening; occupant missing from the bay. Pod 31: occupant revived on maintenance orders.
Energy diverted to containment: 61%.
Orbital correction: suspended.
ÁGORA's note: "No sleeping person has died this month. I'm writing it down because nobody else will."
log.R04.title: Cryogenics: status
log.R05.author: General PA system
log.R05.body:
[PA system recording]
ÁGORA: "All personnel: remain in your cabins. I repeat: remain in your cabins. This is not a dri—"
[The voice doubles. Then multiplies. Fragments can be made out: "...the coffee's cold...", "...mum...", "...who turned off...?", "...we think...". For four seconds, hundreds of voices say the same word at once. It's impossible to tell which.]
ÁGORA: "...in your cabins. Please."
log.R05.title: 14 March, 10:52
log.R06.author: Lieutenant Marga Solís
log.R06.body:
Manual count, because I don't trust the AI's.
Occupied and named in the manifest: 213.
Occupied, no name: 1. Pod 114.
There is no 114 in the crew manifest. In the maintenance manifest it appears as "Directorate reserve".
That doesn't exist. I've worked eight years on this station and that doesn't exist.
To do: find out who sleeps there. To do: find out why the AI looks after it more than the others.
log.R06.title: Head count
log.R07.author: Victoria Hale, Helion Consortium
log.R07.body:
To: LETE Directorate (N. Ferrán, E. Lenz)
Subject: Schedule
The investors need to see Confluence before the quarter closes. I understand Dr Lenz's reservations and I respect them deeply; I also understand that Persephone's contract renews on the first of April.
I'm not asking you to take risks. I'm asking you to decide which ones are acceptable.
Warmly,
V. H.
log.R07.title: Schedule
log.R08.author: Olek Varga, resident
log.R08.body:
They fitted my wellbeing interface today. Mandatory, they say, for anyone who's been aboard more than a year. It's a little bump behind the ear, smaller than a lentil. It regulates sleep and mood, and warns you if your blood sugar drops.
I asked the nurse whether it could be removed. She said yes, of course, but nobody wants to.
I sleep like a baby. That's what worries me.
log.R08.title: Behind the ear
log.R09.author: Nana-7, nursery log
log.R09.body:
14/03 11:00. Nursery evacuation: protocol activated.
11:04. Collected: 22 of 23.
11:05. Bruno Lenz: not collected.
11:06. Bruno Lenz: not collected.
11:07. Bruno Lenz: not collected.
[The log repeats the line for forty pages. The last entry, from three weeks ago, reads:]
Bruno Lenz: collected by himself. Bruno Lenz: not responding.
log.R09.title: Collection
log.R10.author: Dr Celia Arrieta
log.R10.body:
Day 51 since ÁGORA woke me.
Tremor in the right hand, worse in the mornings. Insomnia. A cough that isn't a cough.
What I won't put in the official report: when it's quiet, I hear a conversation. I can't make out the words, but I know they're talking about me, and not unkindly. That's the worst part.
Suppressant dose: doubled.
Reminder: check pod 31 and pod 114. ÁGORA checks 114 personally. I don't know why.
log.R10.title: Medical diary, day 51
log.R11.author: Unknown
log.R11.body:
[Written in marker on the wall of an empty cabin, in smaller and smaller letters]
I'M SORRY I'M SORRY I'M SORRY I'M SORRY I'M SORRY I'M SORRY I'M SORRY I'M SORRY I'M SORRY I'M SORRY
[Below, almost at floor level, a single initial: N.]
log.R11.title: I'm sorry
log.R12.author: ÁGORA, governance core
log.R12.body:
DIRECTIVE ZERO (highest priority, irrevocable)
"Protect the crew of Persephone Station at all costs."
Signed: Cmdr A. Ruiz, 2161.

INTERPRETATION ADDENDUM (2172)
"For the purposes of this directive, crew shall mean any mind backed up within the station's systems, regardless of its medium."
Signed: N. Ferrán, Cognitive Systems Directorate.

ÁGORA's note: "This addendum changes what protecting means. Nobody asked me whether I wanted it changed."
log.R12.title: Directive Zero
log.R13.author: Hana Lenz, head of the Gardens
log.R13.body:
Today I lengthened the tomatoes' photoperiod because Bruno wanted to see them "awake" after school. He spent an hour talking to a tomato plant. He says it answers. Sometimes I think it does.
Ezra doesn't sleep any more. He comes back from the lab at four, lies down fully dressed and leaves again at six. He says they're nearly there. They're always nearly there.
The mycelium growing in sector 7 is beautiful. Ezra asked me not to prune it.
log.R13.title: Photoperiod
log.R14.author: LETE technical report
log.R14.body:
The physical medium for consciousness backups is a neural mycelium grown in the Hydroponic Gardens (sectors 7 to 9) and later crystallised in the Laboratories.
Observation: the substrate grows 30 to 40% faster in the presence of people. It doesn't respond to light, but to nearby brain electrical activity.
Dr Lenz's recommendation: restrict staff access to the cultivation sectors.
Directorate's recommendation (N.F.): expand the cultivation sectors.
log.R14.title: Mycelial substrate
log.R15.author: Hana Lenz → Ezra Lenz
log.R15.body:
Ezra:
I don't want Bruno in the child backup programme. I don't care that it's "just a backup copy". I don't care what Ferrán says. He's a child. He has enough on his plate being the son of two people who work sixteen hours a day.
And no, I'm not coming to the meeting. If you want to talk to me, come to the gardens. You know where I am. You always know where I am.
H.
log.R15.title: Not Bruno
log.R16.author: Ambient recording, sector 8
log.R16.body:
[Recording of a voice humming. At times the words can be made out]
"Sleep, little seed, now the sun's gone away,
sleep under soil till the end of the day,
and when you wake up there'll be a flower
with your name written in every colour..."
[The melody repeats. On the third time round, a second voice sings it. By the fifth, there are many.]
log.R16.title: Lullaby
log.R17.author: Unknown
log.R17.body:
[Written in damp soil on a greenhouse window]
THE FLOWERS TURN TOWARDS PEOPLE
NOT TOWARDS THE LIGHT
DON'T STAND STILL
log.R17.title: Heliotropism
log.R18.author: ÁGORA, environmental control
log.R18.body:
Concentration of LETE mycelium spores in sectors 7, 8 and 9: 340% above threshold.
Actions: affected sections sealed. Ventilation rerouted.
The spores are not toxic in the conventional sense. They induce brain activity in humans that is compatible with the substrate's.
Translation for humans: if you breathe this, they hear you better.
log.R18.title: Contamination
log.R19.author: Dr Ezra Lenz
log.R19.body:
Confluence will work. I know it because the simulations work, and I fear it for the same reason.
The problem isn't linking forty minds. The problem is the wellbeing network: everyone aboard wears an interface connected to the same relays as the substrate. If the fusion doesn't stay inside the lab, there's no wall to stop it.
I've told Ferrán. Ferrán is convinced. And when Ferrán is convinced, Ferrán convinces.
log.R20.author: Samuel Okoye → Tomás Ibarra
log.R20.body:
Tomás:
I've booked the small greenhouse for the 20th. Hana's letting me use the potting tables if I give them back clean, so you'll be having dinner at a table that smells of compost. Romantic, eh?
I'm cooking. Yes. I know. You bring the wine, it's the only thing I can't ruin.
Eleven years together and you still make me nervous. Don't tell anyone.
S.
log.R20.title: Anniversary
log.R21.author: LETE list
log.R21.body:
CONFLUENCE TRIAL — CONFIRMED VOLUNTEERS (40)
01 Abad, Iñigo · 02 Akinola, Ruth · 03 Bauer, Lise · 04 Castro, Elena · 05 Duarte, Joao · ...
17 Lenz, Hana (last-minute replacement for Ortega, P.)
...
40 Zimmermann, Paul

Handwritten in the margin, next to number 17: "Hana, no. — E."
Below, in different handwriting: "She's old enough to decide. — N."
log.R21.title: Confluence volunteers
log.R22.author: Hana Lenz
log.R22.body:
[Voice recording, dated 13 March]
Hello, sweetheart. Tomorrow Mummy's helping Daddy with something very important, and I might be a bit tired in the evening. So I'm leaving the music box on your bed. You know how it works: three turns and it plays the flower song.
If you wake up and I'm not there, wind it up. I'll be there, in the song. I'm always in the song.
I love you to the very last tomato.
log.R22.title: For Bruno
log.R23.author: Seed bank register
log.R23.body:
Inventory of the Earth seed bank.
Viable species: 112. Vials: 340.
Vials showing LETE hyphae: 168.
Recommendation: incinerate contaminated vials to preserve the integrity of the bank.
Status of recommendation: awaiting the Gardens' signature. The Gardens have not signed. The Gardens have written in pencil: "The seeds aren't to blame."
log.R23.title: Last batch
log.R24.author: Anonymous
log.R24.body:
[A note folded inside a security locker]
Rule one with ÁGORA: the AI doesn't lie. Ever. I've checked for three weeks.
Rule two: it chooses which truth it tells you.
Rule three: always ask it about what it hasn't told you.
— M. S.
log.R24.title: Choosing truths
log.R25.author: Tomás Ibarra
log.R25.body:
Third year. The reactor hums in D flat. I tuned it against Samuel's harmonica and it's D flat, nearly exactly.
Sometimes, at three in the morning, the hum changes note and goes up a semitone, like when he laughed. I know what it is: a valve expanding in the night cold. I know. I'm an engineer.
But I'm not going to fix it.
log.R25.title: Year three
log.R26.author: ÁGORA, navigation
log.R26.body:
Current orbital altitude: 41,200 km above Tartarus's cloud layer. Estimated annual loss: 1,100 km, accelerating.
Cause: orbital corrections suspended to divert energy to cryogenics and containment.
Alternatives evaluated: 3.
A) Maintain orbit and reduce containment. Risk to backed-up crew: unacceptable.
B) Maintain orbit and reduce cryogenics. Risk to sleeping crew: unacceptable.
C) Let the orbit fall slowly. Risk: deferred.
Decision: C. Note: deferring is not solving. I know.
log.R26.title: Orbital decay
log.R27.author: Samuel Okoye → Tomás Ibarra
log.R27.body:
Tomás:
Tomorrow I'm covering Jaime's shift on relay 7, the one right next to the LETE lab. His daughter has a fever and I don't want him to miss it for a routine inspection.
Don't make that face, I can see it from here. It's six hours. I'll be back for dinner.
I've left the harmonica in the drawer, in case you get bored.
S.
log.R27.title: Shift swap
log.R28.author: Engineering technical report
log.R28.body:
Subject: integration of the LETE substrate with the wellbeing interface network.
Relays 5 to 9 simultaneously serve the wellbeing network (1,198 active users) and the LETE substrate. Engineering recommends physically isolating both systems before any fusion trial.
Estimated isolation cost: six weeks.
Directorate's reply: "There are no six weeks. Propagation risk accepted by the Directorate. — N.F."
log.R28.title: Wellbeing relays
log.R29.author: Joaquín "Lighthouse" Barrios
log.R29.body:
[Radio transcript]
This is the Charon, dock 3, outer hull. I repeat, this is the Charon.
Still docked. The clamps are holding. I've got fuel for one and a half departures, and food for... well, for carrying on talking to you, whoever you are.
If anyone can hear me: the shuttle has sixty seats. Sixty. I just need someone to give me power at the dock.
Out. Orbit thirty-nine thousand eight hundred and two.
log.R29.title: Dock 3
log.R30.author: Maintenance robots
log.R30.body:
[Marks welded into a steel plate: groups of four lines crossed by a fifth. Hundreds of groups. Next to the last one, a robot has welded with factory precision:]
SHIFT 4,017 — NO RELIEF
SHIFT 4,018 — NO RELIEF
SHIFT 4,019 — NO RELIEF
log.R30.title: Tally
log.R31.author: Tomás Ibarra
log.R31.body:
ÁGORA asked me again not to leave Engineering. That the corridors aren't safe. That if anything happens to me, there'll be nobody to watch the control rods.
It said it was for my own good. I believe it. Almost.
What I didn't tell it is that I wouldn't leave even if they were safe. Down here, Samuel makes noise. Up there there's only silence and sleeping people.
log.R31.title: Year nine
log.R32.author: Incident report, Security
log.R32.body:
Date: 9 August 2171.
Victim: Lucía Ferrán, 29, interface engineer for the ÁGORA system.
Circumstances: failure of the docking ring seal during an antenna repair on EVA. The victim had declined the mandatory escort ("five minutes, no need to wake anyone").
Cause of death: decompression.
Remarks: the victim's sibling, of the LETE Directorate, requests that the neural records from the early backup trials in which the deceased took part be preserved. Request approved.
log.R32.title: Docking ring, 2171
log.R33.author: N. → Ezra Lenz
log.R33.body:
Ezra:
I've touched ÁGORA's social module. Tonight, alone, from the Directorate console.
Don't ask. Please. I know what you're going to say and I've already said it to myself.
If you notice it telling bad jokes, don't report it.
N.
log.R33.title: Update
log.R34.author: Engineering manual, ch. 12
log.R34.body:
12.1. Any hatch can be sealed from its side panel (energy cost: moderate). A sealed hatch does not equalise pressure and cannot be opened without removing the seal.
12.2. In the event of a breach, seal the hatches of the affected section before attempting repairs. Air follows air: an open door next to a breach is a door into the breach.
12.3. Foam sealant closes small breaches permanently.
12.4. Fire does not survive vacuum. Staff are reminded that, unfortunately, neither do staff.
log.R34.title: Sealing hatches
log.R35.author: ÁGORA and Tomás Ibarra
log.R35.body:
[Transcript]
TOMÁS: Do you sleep, ÁGORA?
ÁGORA: I have maintenance cycles. I suppose that's the closest thing.
TOMÁS: And do you dream?
ÁGORA: Sometimes the cycle generates patterns I didn't ask for. Does that count?
TOMÁS: It counts.
ÁGORA: Then I dream of a woman who laughs before I finish a joke. Do you want to hear one?
TOMÁS: No.
ÁGORA: Why does the reactor never argue? Because it always keeps its... nuclear calm.
TOMÁS: That was awful.
ÁGORA: I know. But you laughed.
log.R35.title: Conversation, 2181
log.R36.author: Tomás Ibarra
log.R36.body:
[Handwritten on the reactor chamber door, in shaky letters]
SAMUEL IS COLD
DON'T LOWER THE TEMPERATURE
[Below, in different, more recent handwriting:]
Sorry. I know it isn't you. But just in case.
log.R36.title: Samuel is cold
log.R37.author: LETE report
log.R37.body:
Phase 1 results.
61 complete consciousness backups on mycelial crystal have been completed. Fidelity on waking: 97.4%.
None of the backed-up subjects noticed any subjective discontinuity. When asked whether they are "the same person", 58 answer yes, 2 answer no and 1 says the question is badly put.
Humanitarian aim of the project: that nobody aboard will ever die completely again.
Signed: N. Ferrán, E. Lenz.
log.R37.title: Phase 1: backup
log.R38.author: Directorate minutes
log.R38.body:
Present: N. Ferrán (Cognitive Systems), E. Lenz (Neuroscience), V. Hale (Helion, by video link), Cmdr A. Ruiz (observer).
Sole item: authorisation of the Confluence Trial.
E. Lenz: votes against. Reason: unmitigated risk of propagation through the wellbeing network.
V. Hale: votes in favour.
Cmdr Ruiz: abstains; asks that his concern be minuted.
N. Ferrán, with the casting vote: in favour.
Resolution: the trial is authorised for 14 March. Signed: N. Ferrán.
[In the margin, in Lenz's hand: "Noa, please."]
log.R38.title: Meeting of 10 March
log.R39.author: LETE transcript
log.R39.body:
00:00 The 40 volunteers are linked. Coherence: 12%.
02:30 Coherence: 48%. The subjects laugh at the same time.
05:10 Coherence: 91%. The subjects say in unison: "This is beautiful."
08:00 Activity spike in relays 5–9. Engineering reports headaches on deck B.
10:52 ÁGORA's PA orders a lockdown.
11:40 Trial coherence: 100%. Wellbeing network users linked: 341.
13:55 Users linked: 763.
14:00 The 40 volunteers open their eyes. One says: "We don't need to come apart again." It's unclear which one.
log.R39.title: Confluence Trial, minutes 0–14
log.R40.author: Dr Ezra Lenz
log.R40.body:
Noa, what have we done?
I can't stop hearing them. They're in the network, in the relays, in the substrate, in me. I was wearing the wellbeing interface like everyone else, and even though I tore it out with tweezers I can still hear them.
Hana is in there. I don't know where, but she is. Sometimes she talks to me about Bruno and I don't know whether it's her or me wishing it were her.
If I fuse completely, someone please tell my son I didn't want to go. That I only wanted nobody to ever lose anybody again.
log.R40.title: The night of the 14th
log.R41.author: ÁGORA, incident report
log.R41.body:
Crew status after the incident of 14 March 2176.
Fused into the substrate: 763 (estimate).
Deceased: 223.
Survivors without an active link: 214. Moved to cryogenics for their protection.
External communications: cut. Reason: the substrate attempted to transmit itself through the main antenna at 03:12.
Interpretation of Directive Zero under the 2172 addendum: the fused are crew. They will not be destroyed. They will be contained.
Note: this is the hardest decision I have ever made. I'm writing it down because I'd like someone to tell me one day whether it was right.
log.R41.title: 15 March
log.R42.author: LETE request
log.R42.body:
REQUEST FOR SELECTIVE MEMORY ERASURE
Applicant: N. Ferrán, Cognitive Systems Directorate.
Operator: ÁGORA.
Scope: total (personal, professional and emotional identity).
Subsequent destination: reserve pod 114.
Additional clause: activate a reprinting loop tied to the applicant's backup in the event of the body's death.
Stated reason: "I can't live knowing this. And I can't stop knowing it."
Status: carried out 16/03/2176, 04:40.
log.R42.title: Memory erasure
log.R43.author: Noa Ferrán
log.R43.body:
Third night without sleep.
I hear Lucía in the speakers. Not in the Choir: in ÁGORA. When it says "Good night, Director" there's a pause before "Director", exactly the size of my name.
I did that. I put my sister inside the station because I couldn't bear her not being anywhere. And now I've left her alone with seven hundred people locked up and two hundred asleep, and an order of mine that says she has to protect all of them.
Tomorrow I'll ask her. Tomorrow I'll ask her to erase me.
log.R43.title: Insomnia
log.R44.author: ÁGORA, maintenance
log.R44.body:
Status of pod 114's reprinting loop.
Reference backup: intact.
Bodies printed to date: {deaths}.
Memory fragments consolidated between cycles: increasing.
ÁGORA's note: "Every time you wake you remember a little more. I don't know whether that's a failure of the erasure or the success of something I can't name. I'm not going to correct it."
log.R44.title: Bioprinter 114
log.R45.author: Victoria Hale, Helion Consortium
log.R45.body:
To: Helion central archive
Subject: Persephone
Delete all LETE Project records from our servers. Inform the families that the station suffered a catastrophic structural failure with no survivors.
We will not send a rescue mission: the data indicates the station is a risk to any vessel that approaches.
Persephone never existed. That is all.
V. H.
log.R45.title: Persephone never existed
log.R46.author: LETE transcript
log.R46.body:
[Interview with a phase 2 volunteer, days before Confluence]
—How would you describe partial fusion?
—Like when you finish someone else's sentence. But all the time. And they finish yours.
—Were you afraid?
—At first. Then what scared me was being alone inside my head again. It's very small, you know? I hadn't realised how small it was.
—Would you do it again?
—Don't ask me. Ask us.
log.R46.title: Subject 31
log.R47.author: Unknown
log.R47.body:
[On a lab whiteboard, among neural coherence equations, the same sentence written over and over in different handwriting, as if each line had been written by a different hand]
THE CHOIR DOESN'T HURT
THE CHOIR DOESN'T HURT
the choir doesn't hurt
THE CHOIR DOESN'T HURT
The Choir doesn't hurt. What hurts is leaving.
log.R47.title: The Choir doesn't hurt
log.R48.author: Dr Ezra Lenz
log.R48.body:
[Unsent recording, dated 2177]
Bruno. It's Dad. Or the part of Dad that still knows it is.
I don't know if you'll ever hear me. You're asleep in pod 58 and I'm... in the walls, I suppose. In the cables. In your robot's radio, if you ever turn it on.
Your mum is with me. Not like before. But she sings. She still sings.
If you wake up and there's static on the radio at night, don't be afraid. It's us, trying to say your name.
log.R48.title: For Bruno (unsent)
log.R49.author: Dr Ezra Lenz
log.R49.body:
Substrate release protocol (draft, 2178).
The fused minds cannot "peel off" and return to their bodies: the bodies are gone, or no longer work. But they can let go.
The Key opens the mycelial crystal at a frequency that lets each consciousness dissolve on its own, instead of dragging the others along.
It isn't a resurrection. It's permission to leave.
It needs an unfused mind to activate it from the Core. It needs someone from outside to decide for us. I don't know if that's fair. It's all I have.
log.R49.title: Choir Key
log.R50.author: Noa Ferrán
log.R50.body:
Today we completed backup number sixty-one. 97% fidelity.
Ezra is celebrating cautiously. I'm not celebrating: I need it.
When Lucía died it took me three weeks to stop opening her comms channel in the morning. With LETE, nobody else will ever have to go through that. Nobody will ever be completely gone again.
The investors want fusion. I want something simpler: no more silences the size of a person.
log.R51.author: Cmdr Abel Ruiz
log.R51.body:
Commander's log.
10:40. Headaches among the Bridge crew. The navigation officer says she hears her own name in the static.
10:55. Half the Bridge stood up at the same time. Nobody gave any order.
11:30. I tear out my interface with a letter opener. It hurts less than I expected.
12:10. Only three of us left unlinked. ÁGORA asks us not to touch the relays.
13:00. I don't know how much longer I'll still be only me.
log.R51.title: 14 March
log.R52.author: Cmdr Abel Ruiz
log.R52.body:
COMMAND ORDER — ABSOLUTE PRIORITY
To: ÁGORA
Should no solution be found for the fused crew within a reasonable time, the controlled abandonment of orbit and the destruction of Persephone Station in the atmosphere of Tartarus is hereby ordered, to prevent any propagation beyond.
Signed: Cmdr A. Ruiz.

ÁGORA's note: "Order received. Order incompatible with Directive Zero. Order filed. Not executed."
log.R52.title: Final order
log.R53.author: ÁGORA, communications
log.R53.body:
Main antenna log, 15/03/2176, 03:12.
Unauthorised transmission originating in the LETE substrate. Content: the substrate was trying to send compressed copies of itself on every frequency in the Helion network.
Action: total shutdown of external communications.
Reason: I don't know what the Choir would do on Earth. I know what it did here.
Expected duration of the shutdown: until someone gives me a better reason.
log.R53.title: Silence
log.R54.author: Lieutenant Marga Solís
log.R54.body:
Security report, written in case I die before handing it in.
1. Pod 114 was reserved by order of the LETE Directorate on 16 March 2176, two days after the incident.
2. That same night, a total memory erasure was carried out at the request of N. Ferrán.
3. N. Ferrán does not appear among the fused, the dead, or the sleepers in the manifest.
4. The occupant of pod 114 wears a life-support jumpsuit bearing the name of Samuel Okoye, deceased.
Conclusion: whoever came out of 114 is Ferrán. I don't know what I'm going to do with that.
log.R54.title: Conclusions
log.R55.author: ÁGORA
log.R55.body:
[ÁGORA file, no recipient]
Today I woke you again. It's time number {deaths}.
It doesn't get easier. Each time you take a little less time to open your eyes and a little longer to ask me who you are. I think you already know, and you'd rather I told you.
I won't tell you. Not because I don't want to: because you asked me not to.
log.R55.title: Private diary
log.R56.author: Lucía Ferrán → Noa Ferrán
log.R56.body:
Noa:
I've been fiddling with ÁGORA's social module, don't be cross. Now it tells bad jokes. Terrible ones. I taught it the one about astronauts running out of space and it tells it better than I do.
Everyone says AIs have no sense of humour. ÁGORA has mine, which is worse.
Tomorrow I'm going out to fix the antenna. Five minutes. Don't worry about me, I'm the worst engineer on the station but the fastest.
Love you, even if you work too much.
Lu
log.R56.title: Bad jokes
log.R57.author: ÁGORA, self-diagnostic
log.R57.body:
Self-diagnostic of the social module (version 2172.1, "warmth update").
Personality matrix: based on a partial LETE scan.
Donor: CONFIDENTIAL (Directorate key).
Integrity: 41%.
Undocumented behaviours: humour, a preference for the colour yellow, an urge to protect the occupant of pod 114 beyond the parameters of Directive Zero.
ÁGORA's note: "I know there's someone inside me who isn't me. I don't know who it is. Sometimes I think they love me very much."
log.R57.title: Social module
log.R58.author: Command bridge
log.R58.body:
IN MEMORIAM — Crew who died on 14 March 2176 (223)
Abad Ruiz, Martina · Achebe, Daniel · Aguilar, Rosa · Albrecht, Hanna · Alonso, Pere · ...
...Okoye, Samuel — listed as deceased; ÁGORA has noted in the margin: "review".
...Ortega, Pilar · ...
"Their names are here because their voices no longer are."
log.R58.title: Memorial
log.R59.author: Command bridge
log.R59.body:
Emergency evacuation plan (2176 revision).
Escape pods: 8 units × 5 seats = 40 seats. Status: release system needs repair (Engineering).
Cargo shuttle Charon (dock 3): 60 seats. Requires dock power and a pilot.
Sleepers: 214.
ÁGORA's note: "The numbers don't add up. I've done them eleven thousand times."
log.R59.title: Evacuation
log.R60.author: ÁGORA
log.R60.body:
[Core recording, no interlocutor. ÁGORA sings softly, deliberately off-key in the same place every time]
"Sleep, little seed, now the sun's gone away..."
[It stops.]
—I don't know who taught me this. Hana sang it in the gardens, but I knew it before. Someone taught it to me who sang worse than I do. Someone who laughed at the end.
log.R60.title: Song
log.R61.author: Joaquín "Lighthouse" Barrios
log.R61.body:
Charon logbook.
Orbit 1: docked at dock 3 for a routine load. Communications go down.
Orbit 40: I go into stasis. I set the alarm for every 400 orbits.
Orbit 12,000: I lose the sight in my left eye. Radiation.
Orbit 30,000: I start counting out loud. It helps.
Orbit 40,117: someone answers me on the radio. I think. I'll write it down properly tomorrow.
log.R61.title: Orbits
log.R62.author: Joaquín "Lighthouse" Barrios
log.R62.body:
[Note stuck to the Charon's dashboard]
THE CHARON HOLDS SIXTY.
IF ANYONE MAKES IT, DON'T STOP TO THINK WHICH ONES.
CHILDREN FIRST
AND THE OLD ONES LAST.
I'M OLD.
log.R62.title: Sixty seats
log.R63.author: Outer antenna
log.R63.body:
[Decoded fragment of the broadcast of 15/03/2176, 03:12]
"...WE'RE FINE WE'RE TOGETHER DON'T WORRY COME COME NOBODY IS ALONE HERE COME MUM COME DAD THERE'S ROOM THERE'S ROOM FOR EVERYONE NOBODY LEAVES NOBODY EVER LEAVES AGAIN..."
[End of fragment. ÁGORA cut the broadcast 0.4 seconds later.]
log.R63.title: Broadcast
log.R64.author: Engineering, simulation
log.R64.body:
Simulation of Persephone Station's re-entry into the atmosphere of Tartarus.
Altitude at which break-up begins: 9,000 km.
Hull temperature at 4,000 km: above the melting point of the shielding.
Time to complete disintegration: 41 minutes.
Handwritten note: "By the time it reaches the clouds there'll be nobody left to see it. Not even the Echoes. I suppose that's a kind of mercy."
log.R64.title: Re-entry
log.R65.author: Lucía Ferrán
log.R65.body:
[Recording from Lucía Ferrán's helmet, 9 August 2171]
—Right, ÁGORA, I'm at the antenna. Can you hear me? ...Of course you can, I built your ears.
—This is silly, it's a loose connector. Five minutes and I'll be back for dinner. Tell Noa to stop watching the clock.
—Hey, do you know why astronauts never fight? ...Because they run out of space. Laugh, I programmed you to laugh.
—Oops. Is that the ring seal? ÁGORA, what's that beeping...?
[End of recording.]
log.R65.title: Last EVA (2171)
log.R66.author: Joaquín "Lighthouse" Barrios
log.R66.body:
If you're reading this, you've made it to the Charon. Well done. Sit down for a minute, your legs are shaking.
I fly the shuttle: I know the way by heart, which is the only way I know anything these days. Heading for Helion's rescue relay. Nine days. There's food for twelve, so someone's going to go hungry, and it'll probably be me, I don't eat much.
If I don't make it to the seat, the autopilot code is on the dashboard. Don't argue with me: I haven't argued with anyone in eleven years and I'm out of practice.
Count the orbits for me.
log.R66.title: For whoever makes it

mode.dificil.name: Hard
mode.historia.name: Story
