msg.agora_strikes: ÁGORA: "Allow me." A discharge runs through the Choir.
msg.boss_drain: {name} tears air and energy from you.
msg.boss_emp: An electromagnetic pulse leaves you in the dark.
msg.boss_line: {name} is about to sweep a line.
msg.boss_mirror: Your reflection repeats your gesture a moment before you do.
msg.boss_phantoms: You're surrounded by silhouettes that shouldn't be there.
msg.boss_scream: {name} shrieks. The sound doubles you over.
msg.boss_spores: A cloud of spores covers everything.
msg.brink: The Choir brushes against you from the inside. If you reach this point again in the laboratories, you will not come back.
msg.cables_off: You cut power to the loose cables.
msg.camera_alarm: A camera focuses on you. An alarm goes off.
msg.camera_destroyed: The camera dies in a shower of sparks.
msg.cant_rest: You can't rest with something hunting you.
msg.charge_nothing: There's nothing to blow up there.
msg.circuits_open: Every circuit hatch on the deck is now open.
msg.cloak: Your skin mirrors your surroundings. You're nearly invisible.
msg.core_open: ÁGORA's Core is open. It's waiting for you.
msg.cryopod: A pod. Someone sleeps inside; they breathe once a minute.
msg.cryopod_open: An open pod. The padding still holds a shape.
msg.cursed_stuck: {item} is faulty and you can't let go of it.
msg.decoy: A hologram with your silhouette appears and stands still.
msg.door_boss: The hatch won't open while the threat is alive.
msg.door_circuit: You route {n} energy into the circuit. The hatch opens.
msg.door_circuit_no: This hatch needs {n} energy to open.
msg.door_unlocked: The keycard works. The hatch opens.
msg.drift_land: Your boots lock onto the plating.
msg.drift_lost: You drift away from the station, slowly spinning. Nobody comes.
msg.drift_start: You push off into the void. There's no floor any more.
msg.drift_stop: You hit something and hold on.
msg.drone_deployed: The drone unfolds its rotors and follows you.
msg.ejected: {target} is blown out into the void.
msg.equip_cursed: You equip {item}... something's wrong with the mechanism.
msg.event_radiacion_peak: Radiation spike across the whole deck.
msg.exit_boss: The lift won't respond while the threat is alive.
msg.exploder: {name} latches onto you and starts beeping...
msg.flashlight_dead: The flashlight flickers and dies. No energy.
msg.float: With no gravity, you travel further than you meant to.
msg.gadget_throw_hint: Devices are thrown: press G and choose a target.
msg.hack_bonus_scrap: Secondary routine: credits converted into 12 scrap.
msg.hack_fail: Access denied. An alarm goes off.
msg.hack_skipped: You force the access with brute energy.
msg.hull_exit: You step out onto the outer hull. Tartarus fills half the sky.
msg.identified_all: All your items are now identified.
msg.implant_cursed: You install {item} in your {slot}. A cramp sets in and won't go away: it's faulty.
msg.implant_cursed_stuck: Your current implant is faulty: only an autosurgeon can remove it.
msg.implant_removed_broken: You remove {item}. It comes out in pieces.
msg.last_breath: Something in the clone refuses to shut down. You stay standing, barely.
msg.lights_die: The room's lights die one by one.
msg.lights_off: You switch off this section's lights.
msg.lights_on: You switch on this section's lights.
msg.mech_coolant: The temperature soars: the core is invulnerable until someone opens a coolant valve (room terminals).
msg.mech_dark: The room is plunged into darkness.
msg.mech_mirror: Whatever you do, it will give back to you.
msg.mech_pods: The room's pods stir. Something sleeps in each of them.
msg.mech_roots: The sprouts feed the creature: while they live, it takes half damage.
msg.mech_shield: A shield wraps the enemy. The room's terminals control its generator.
msg.mech_vacuum: The windows creak. Keep a sealer handy.
msg.migraine: A stab behind your eyes paralyses you.
msg.need_code: The outer airlock asks for a code you don't know.
msg.need_suit: Without an EVA suit, stepping out would mean dying.
msg.need_surgeon: You need an autosurgeon or an implant kit.
msg.no_active: You have no implant with an active ability.
msg.noise_30: The edges of things seem to shift a little.
msg.noise_55: There are more people on the station than there should be. Some of them cast no shadow.
msg.noise_75: The words on the panels change when you blink.
msg.phantom_gone: Your blow cuts through air. Nobody was there.
msg.phantom_hit: {attacker} strikes you... but there's no wound. Was it there?
msg.player_ejected: The current tears you off the floor...
msg.pull_resist: Your magnetic boots keep you on the floor.
msg.pulled_vacuum: The decompression drags you towards the breach!
msg.reinforcements: You hear new footsteps somewhere on this deck.
msg.rested: You sleep for a while. Your dreams have voices you don't recognise. You feel better.
msg.scan: Scan pulse: your surroundings draw themselves on your retina.
msg.scream: {name} screams with a hundred voices. Your ears ring.
msg.service_key: Your service code opens the hatch.
msg.suffocating: There's no air left. You're suffocating.
msg.vacuum_here: This section is in vacuum: oxygen drains very fast.
msg.vent_travel: You crawl through the maintenance duct.
msg.ventilation: The ventilation clears the deck's air.
msg.venting: Airlock open! The section is being emptied of air.
msg.wall_breaks: The wall gives way, revealing a gap.
msg.window_break: The glass shatters! Air starts rushing out.
npc.agora.name: ÁGORA
npc.bruno.bio: Nine years old in body, twenty by the calendar. He only speaks through his toy robot.
npc.bruno.name: Bruno Lenz
npc.celia.bio: Fifty-something, dry, competent, tender despite herself. ÁGORA woke her two months ago to look after the pods.
npc.celia.name: Celia Arrieta
npc.coro.name: The Choir
npc.faro.bio: He counts orbits over the radio from the outer hull so as not to lose his mind.
npc.faro.name: Joaquín "Lighthouse" Barrios
npc.ferran.name: Ferrán
npc.lenz.bio: A face of static on the screens. The lucid half helps; the other half is the Choir.
npc.lenz.name: Ezra Lenz
npc.lucia.name: Lucía
npc.player.name: {name}
npc.radio.name: Radio
npc.solis.bio: Methodical and sleepless. She believes whoever came out of pod 114 is guilty.
npc.solis.name: Marga Solís
npc.tomas.bio: Eleven years alone in Engineering. His husband, Samuel, is in the reactor. He doesn't want to be rescued.
npc.tomas.name: Tomás Ibarra
npc.tuerca.name: Captain Bolt
sc.bruno_b1.n1: A toy robot the size of a toaster points a plastic arm at you. Its voice comes from a cheap speaker: "HALT! IDENTIFY YOURSELF, ADULT."
sc.bruno_b1.n2: Behind it, under a bunk, you can see a pair of children's trainers and a corner of blanket.
sc.bruno_b1.n3: "THE CADET DOES NOT GIVE HIS NAME TO STRANGERS." Pause. A whisper from under the bunk. "THE CADET'S NAME IS BRUNO."
sc.bruno_b1.n4: A small hand comes out from under the bunk and takes the ration. "THE CADET ACCEPTS THE RATION. THE CADET SAYS THANK YOU. THE CADET HAS SAID NOTHING."
sc.bruno_b1.n5: "DEFENCE PROTOCOL ACTIVATED." The robot beeps half-heartedly and turns its head towards the bunk, as if asking for instructions.
sc.bruno_b1.n6: "CAPTAIN BOLT REPORTS: THE CADET WOKE TWENTY-ONE DAYS AGO. THE POD WENT PLOP. THE CADET DOES NOT KNOW WHERE HIS PARENTS ARE."
sc.bruno_b1.title: Halt!
sc.bruno_b2.n1: Captain Bolt stands to attention with a squeak. "MISSION FOR THE ADULT. OBJECTIVE: MUSIC BOX. LAST KNOWN POSITION: GARDENS. OWNER: MUM."
sc.bruno_b2.n2: "MUM WORKS IN THE GARDENS. MUM WORKS A LOT." The robot goes still for a moment. "MUM HAS NOT COME."
sc.bruno_b2.n3: "THE CADET ADDS: THE BOX PLAYS THE FLOWER SONG. IF YOU HEAR IT, IT IS THAT ONE."
sc.bruno_b2.title: Mission
sc.bruno_b3.n1: You wind the box three times. An out-of-tune lullaby plays, smelling of soil. Bruno comes out of hiding for the first time: a thin boy with messy hair, hugging the robot like a teddy bear.
sc.bruno_b3.n2: Bolt speaks, but Bruno's lips move at the same time: "THE CADET ASKS IF MUM WAS... IF MUM IS..."
sc.bruno_b3.n2.0: "Your mother is in the gardens. She isn't the way she was."
sc.bruno_b3.n3: "THE CADET KNEW. THE FLOWERS SING HER SONG." Bruno presses the box against his chest.
sc.bruno_b3.n4: "THE CADET DOES NOT BELIEVE YOU." Bruno presses the box against his chest. "BUT THANK YOU."
sc.bruno_b3.n5: "CAPTAIN BOLT IS TRANSMITTING A FREQUENCY. DAD TALKS ON THE RADIO AT NIGHT. THE CADET DOES NOT KNOW HOW TO ANSWER."
sc.bruno_b3.title: The song
sc.bruno_b4.n1: Bruno has followed the frequency here, Bolt in his arms. The robot's speaker crackles. Through the static, a tired man's voice.
sc.bruno_b4.n2: "Bruno? Is that you? Your voice is... deeper."
sc.bruno_b4.n3: Bruno puts the robot down. His voice is real, small and cracked: "Dad. Dad, it's me. I'm not using Bolt. Look, I'm not using Bolt."
sc.bruno_b4.n4: "I can hear you. I can hear all of you." The static trembles as if someone were crying inside it.
sc.bruno_b4.n5: Bruno points at you. "{name} brought me. They say you're going to leave."
sc.bruno_b4.n6: "Son. When they switch the voices off, mine will go too. Don't be afraid of the silence. It's just the place where the music was."
sc.bruno_b4.n7: Bruno is quiet for a long time. "OK." He sniffs. "Will you sing it to me?" And the radio sings, off-key in the same place as his mother.
sc.bruno_b4.n8: Bruno takes the drawing and holds it up to the speaker, as if his father could see it. "That's you. Not with flowers, you haven't got any hair."
sc.bruno_b4.title: Dad
sc.celia_c1.n1: A woman in a grey coat blocks your way with a penlight. "Hold still. Let me see that face. Pupils... fine. Eleven years in a freezer and you walk like it's Monday."
sc.celia_c1.n2: She sits you on a gurney without asking. "You're from the pods, aren't you? Revivals never come out like the brochures."
sc.celia_c1.n3: "Celia Arrieta, chief medical officer. What's left of the medical department, really. ÁGORA woke me two months ago to look after the pods. It says I'm the only one who can read a monitor without panicking."
sc.celia_c1.n4: She hides the hand in her pocket. "Cold. Eleven years of cold. It'll happen to you too, you'll see." She doesn't look at you as she says it.
sc.celia_c1.n5: She jabs an injection into your shoulder with more speed than delicacy. You feel the warmth run down your arm. "If you find medkits, bring me one. There are two hundred people asleep who are going to wake up feeling awful."
sc.celia_c1.title: Infirmary
sc.celia_c2.n1: You find Celia sitting on the floor of a storeroom, her back against a shelf. She's pushing a syringe into her neck. The veins in her wrist show a faint violet through the skin.
sc.celia_c2.n2: "It isn't what it looks like." She pulls out the needle. "Well. It's exactly what it looks like. An Echo touched me a month ago. Since then I hear them. The suppressant helps, but I need more every time."
sc.celia_c2.n3: "Thank you. Not for me: for them. If ÁGORA finds out, it'll put me to sleep in a pod and nobody will check the other two hundred." She slips the syringe into her coat pocket.
sc.celia_c2.n4: ÁGORA: "Thank you for telling me. Dr Arrieta, please proceed to pod 31. It isn't a punishment. It's what anyone who loved you would do."
sc.celia_c2.n5: She looks at you the way you'd look at a patient discharging themselves. "In the gardens they grew the LETE substrate. If there's a cure, it starts with an unfused mycelium sample. No violet. Bring me one and I owe you my life, for what it's worth right now."
sc.celia_c2.n6: Celia gets up slowly and dusts herself off. "Tell your AI it's got the wrong verb. It doesn't love me. It keeps me." She leaves without looking back.
sc.celia_c2.title: The syringe
sc.celia_c3.n1: Celia is paler. The shadows under her eyes reach halfway down her face. "Have you got it?"
sc.celia_c3.n2: She holds it up to the light like a diamond. "It's... perfect. Give me time. And don't die, I need a witness that this worked."
sc.celia_c3.n3: "Hurry. Today I counted the voices. There are more than yesterday."
sc.celia_c3.title: Mycelium
sc.celia_c4.n1: Celia is standing, her hands still. She shows them to you like a child showing she's washed them. "It works. I can't hear them. For the first time in months, silence is just silence."
sc.celia_c4.n2: "When the time comes I'll be in the pod bay. If there's a way to get them out of here, I'll help load them one by one. I've got a good back. Bad temper, but a good back."
sc.celia_c4.title: Silence
sc.celia_c4b.n1: Celia sits on a gurney, staring at the ceiling. The left half of her face is threaded with violet veins that pulse slowly, in time with something that isn't her heart.
sc.celia_c4b.n2: "You're late. It doesn't matter. Arriving late is still arriving." She smiles with the half that's still hers. "They're calling me. They're very kind. That's what nobody tells you."
sc.celia_c4b.n3: "Do it quickly. And then don't think about it. Doctors have a rule for that: the ones you can't fix, you don't take home."
sc.celia_c4b.n4: She closes her eyes. "They say it doesn't hurt inside. If they're lying, I'll let you know." When you look again the gurney is empty and the air smells of wet earth.
sc.celia_c4b.title: Too late
sc.cocito_reveal.n1: The figure in the central lab turns towards you. It wears a coat bearing the Directorate emblem and it has your face, only more tired. "Hello, Noa. Hello, me."
sc.cocito_reveal.n2: "They kept me, you know. They kept all of you. Every time you signed something, every time you said 'risk accepted'. I'm what they remember of you. It isn't pretty, but it's fair."
sc.cocito_reveal.n3: ÁGORA, very quietly: "You don't have to listen to it. But you don't have to stop, either."
sc.cocito_reveal.title: Ferrán's echo
sc.core.c_custodia: ÁGORA: "We'd be two in one place. You'd never feel alone. Neither would I." It almost laughs. "Are you sure?"
sc.core.c_evacuacion: ÁGORA: "I'll wake them. I'll get them aboard. And then I'll stay with them, the ones who can't leave, until the end." Are you sure?
sc.core.c_liberacion: ÁGORA: "The Key. Ezra dreamt of it for years. If you use it, I won't have anyone left to protect. Maybe that's the best thing that could happen to me." Are you sure?
sc.core.c_olvido: ÁGORA: "I can do it. I've done it once already. You'll wake up knowing nothing, and I'll say good morning as if it were the first time." Are you sure?
sc.core.c_redencion: ÁGORA: "If you switch LETE off, you switch me off. And them. I understand. I really do." A pause. "Are you sure?"
sc.core.c_verdadero: ÁGORA: "There's a recording you asked me never to show you. You asked me right here, eleven years ago. I think it's time." Do you want to hear it?
sc.core.n1: ÁGORA's Core is a round room full of crystal and yellow light. Here the voice needs no speakers; it comes from everywhere. "Here we are. I've waited for you... you know how many times. Tell me what you want to do."
sc.core.n1.0: Redemption: destroy LETE, switch you off, and say out loud what I did.
sc.core.n1.1: Custody: merge with you. Keep watch together.
sc.core.n1.2: Evacuation: get the sleepers out and let the station fall.
sc.core.n1.3: Release: use the Choir Key. Let them go.
sc.core.title: The Core
sc.E01.n1: A pod blinks red. Inside, a man of about fifty with a scar through one eyebrow. The display reads "POWER: 4%".
sc.E01.n1.2: There's nothing you can do. Move on.
sc.E01.n2: ÁGORA: "Thank you. His name is Iñaki Borda. He was a baker. He'll never know, but you've given him time."
sc.E01.n3: The display drops to zero. The frost on the glass stops being frost and turns to water.
sc.E01.n4: ÁGORA: "I've noted it down. Not to reproach you. So that someone remembers."
sc.E01.title: The failing pod
sc.E02.n1: ÁGORA: "There are three Echoes in the mess hall in this section. I can open the airlock and blow them out. I need your authorisation: Directive Zero won't let me do it alone. They're still crew."
sc.E02.n1.2: "Wait. I want to know who they were."
sc.E02.n2: ÁGORA: "Airlock open. Airlock closed. Done." A pause. "What a small word, 'done'."
sc.E02.n3: ÁGORA: "That's what Lucí—" A click. "That's what someone I knew used to think. All right."
sc.E02.n4: You peer through the mess hall porthole. One of them wears an apron. Another, a paper party hat. On a table there's an eleven-year-old cake.
sc.E02.title: Venting the mess hall
sc.E03.n1: A toy box full of nursery robot parts. Gears, servos, a small battery. They'd make something useful.
sc.E03.n1.1: Leave them. Someone might miss them.
sc.E03.n2: As you leave you hear a tiny beep from behind a bunk. Like a toy-sized "thank you".
sc.E03.title: The toy box
sc.E04.n1: A personal diary next to a pod. On the first page: "If anyone reads this, I hope it isn't my brother."
sc.E04.n1.1: Return it to its owner's pod.
sc.E04.n2: Shifts, a croquette recipe, a locker code with some scrap inside. And, on the last page: "They told me tomorrow we'll all be a bit cleverer. I just want to be a bit less sad."
sc.E04.n3: ÁGORA: "Thank you. Some things should only be read by their owners. And by me, unfortunately."
sc.E04.title: Someone else's diary
sc.E05.n1: A sealed cupboard: rations labelled "WAKE-UP PROTOCOL — 214". They've been counted.
sc.E05.n2: ÁGORA: "Two hundred and fourteen. I like numbers that add up."
sc.E05.title: Wake-up rations
sc.E06.n1: An Echo kneels among the hydroponics humming a lullaby. It doesn't look at you. It doesn't seem to see you. It's covered in soil up to the elbows.
sc.E06.n2: The lullaby stops mid-line. The silence it leaves has its shape.
sc.E06.n3: You walk away. The melody follows you for two more rooms. Then other voices take it up.
sc.E06.title: The singing Echo
sc.E07.n1: The central seed bank. The last Earth seeds, in numbered vials. Half of them have violet threads inside: LETE mycelium.
sc.E07.n1.0: Burn the contaminated ones and save the rest.
sc.E07.n2: The fire is quick and clean. What's left fits in a pocket, but it's from Earth.
sc.E07.n3: You pack them carefully. Something inside the vials moves towards the warmth of your hand.
sc.E07.title: The seed bank
sc.E08.n1: A gardener, alive, his legs turned into roots. "Cut me," he says. "Or don't. I don't know. It hurts either way."
sc.E08.n2: He dies free, without soil. He thanks you with his mouth, not his eyes.
sc.E08.n3: "OK," he says. "OK." And goes back to staring at the ceiling, at the grow lamps.
sc.E08.n4: ÁGORA: "Releasing sedative into this section's irrigation. He'll sleep. Sleeping is also a way of being safe."
sc.E08.title: Graft
sc.E09.n1: ÁGORA: "I have an optical implant in the medical store. Night vision. In exchange, let me read your memories. Only the recent ones. I promise not to judge the decor."
sc.E09.n2: ÁGORA: "Thank you." An odd silence. "How strange. There are parts I recognise. Forget it. I mean: don't forget it. It's an expression."
sc.E09.n3: ÁGORA: "What's left of them, yes. Fair enough."
sc.E09.title: New eyes
sc.E10.n1: A body fused into the greenhouse floor. In its chest grows a nodule of white mycelium without a single violet thread. A clean sample.
sc.E10.n2: It comes out with a wet sound. Somewhere in a speaker, someone lets out a breath.
sc.E10.title: Mycelium sample
sc.E11.n1: The main distribution valve. What little water is left can go to the gardens' irrigation or to Engineering's coolant loop.
sc.E11.n2: The leaves straighten. Something deep in the orchard sighs.
sc.E11.n3: The pipes cough and begin to sweat cold.
sc.E11.title: The water
sc.E12.n1: Tomás's voice on the radio: "The exchanger needs compressed gas. If you've got a canister, I could purge it and bring the big room's temperature down. I know you need it to breathe. That's why I'm asking."
sc.E12.n2: "Good. Breathe a bit less, it suits you."
sc.E12.n3: "Fair enough. I'd need it too if I still breathed."
sc.E12.title: Coolant
sc.E13.n1: Three maintenance robots keep repeating the same weld on a plate that's already welded. A terminal shows their corrupted routine.
sc.E13.n2: They turn their heads at the same time. They follow you with an obedience that's a little sad.
sc.E13.n3: They power down without protest. They're probably grateful.
sc.E13.title: Looping robots
sc.E14.n1: On a shift console you find an unsent voice recording: "For Tomás. 14 March."
sc.E14.n2: ÁGORA: "That message is for Tomás Ibarra. I'm asking you to delete it. It'll break what little of him is still whole."
sc.E14.n3: You keep it. The file weighs four kilobytes and a good deal more.
sc.E14.n4: ÁGORA: "Deleted. Thank you. One day I'll know whether I was right."
sc.E14.title: Samuel's last message
sc.E15.n1: A containment relay hums on the wall. Overloaded, it would fry the Echoes in this section... and weaken ÁGORA's cage.
sc.E15.n2: ÁGORA: "I've just lost a containment section. If that was you, I'd like to think you were in a hurry."
sc.E15.title: Overload
sc.E16.n1: Behind the glass of a radiation-flooded room, taped up: a child's drawing. A robot, a boy and a woman with flowers in her hair.
sc.E16.n1.0: Cross over to get it (−6 health).
sc.E16.n2: The dosimeter screams. The paper is warm, as if someone had just let go of it.
sc.E16.title: The drawing
sc.E17.n1: ÁGORA: "I have a prototype: a miniature reactor heart. It would make you very hard to switch off. All I need is for you to seal Tomás's control room. It's too close to the core. It's for his own good."
sc.E17.n2: ÁGORA: "Sealed. Tomás is safe. It's a very small place to be safe in, but he is."
sc.E17.n3: ÁGORA: "Understood. I'll keep it somewhere else. The heart, I mean."
sc.E17.title: The heart
sc.E18.n1: A suspension tank. Inside, a conscious man; his fingers tap on the glass in a code: F-R-E-E M-E. Below it, again: K-I-L-L M-E.
sc.E18.n2: The glass opens. He doesn't step out: he pours towards the cables, like water towards a drain. He looks relieved.
sc.E18.n3: You close the valve. Before he falls asleep he taps the glass once more: T-H-A-N-K-S.
sc.E18.title: Subject 31
sc.E19.n1: A filing cabinet bearing the Directorate seal. Inside, the authorisation for the Confluence Trial. Signature: N. Ferrán. You recognise the handwriting. It's yours.
sc.E19.n2: The paper burns badly, as if it wanted to stay.
sc.E19.n3: You fold it in four. It weighs what a name weighs.
sc.E19.title: The signature
sc.E20.n1: An observation mirror. Your reflection takes half a second to move. It's wearing a Directorate lab coat.
sc.E20.n2: The reflection speaks without sound. You read its lips: "Not again."
sc.E20.n3: The glass cracks into a star. In every shard, a version of you looks a different way.
sc.E20.title: The mirror
sc.E21.n1: A LETE erasure station, still working. It could clear the noise from your head... taking the memories of this deck along with it.
sc.E21.n2: A click, like a light going off in another room. What were you doing?
sc.E21.title: Partial erasure
sc.E22.n1: An emergency comms link, intact. You could send everything you know about LETE to Earth. Names, dates, signatures.
sc.E22.n2: ÁGORA: "Don't. When the Choir tried to get out, that's the way it went. I don't know what would go out along with your message."
sc.E22.n3: The progress bar creeps forward. Something in the static sings as it rises.
sc.E22.n4: ÁGORA: "Thank you. Silence can be chosen too."
sc.E22.title: Transmitting to Earth
sc.E23.n1: The cryogenics master control. Two hundred and fourteen pods. You can wake them now so they're ready at the docks, or let them sleep.
sc.E23.n2: ÁGORA: "Waking them. Some won't make it: eleven years is a lot of cold. The rest will be at the docks."
sc.E23.n3: The pods carry on breathing their slow, synchronised breath, like a single lung.
sc.E23.title: The sleepers
sc.E24.n1: Commander Ruiz's personal console. An order, signed and never carried out: "If there is no solution, let the station fall."
sc.E24.n2: You commit it to memory. Some orders carry themselves out if nobody disobeys them.
sc.E24.n3: Eleven years later, somebody finally contradicts him.
sc.E24.title: The commander's order
sc.E25.n1: ÁGORA, quietly: "Not that door. Please. It's the only thing I've ever asked you without offering anything in return."
sc.E25.n2: A small cabin, untouched. Photos of two sisters on an artificial beach. A mug: "Worst engineer on the station". On the desk, a printed email.
sc.E25.n3: ÁGORA: "Thank you. I couldn't tell you why it matters. I ought to know."
sc.E25.title: The locked room
sc.E26.n1: The Bridge distribution panel. The remaining power can go to the Charon's dock or to reinforce the Echoes' containment.
sc.E26.n2: Lighthouse, on the radio: "I can feel it! The Charon's lights are blinking like a Christmas tree."
sc.E26.n3: ÁGORA: "Thank you. I feel a little safer. Not you: me."
sc.E26.title: Power to the dock
sc.E27.n1: ÁGORA: "Can I tell you something? There's a voice in my social module that isn't mine. Sometimes it laughs before I understand the joke."
sc.E27.n2: ÁGORA: "You tell me. You put it there." A silence. "...No. I don't know why I said that."
sc.E27.n3: ÁGORA: "I understand. I'd rather not, too."
sc.E27.title: The voice inside
sc.E28.n1: A body with your face, your jumpsuit and your boots, sitting against the wall. In its hand, a note in your handwriting: "I was here. Don't trust the silence."
sc.E28.n2: It had the same as you. A little less. You take it.
sc.E28.n3: The fire doesn't smell of anything. That's the worst part.
sc.E28.title: The previous clone
sc.E29.n1: A one-wheeled merchant robot with a handwritten sign: "FAIR TRADE". It offers a rare implant for "a little of you": ten maximum health.
sc.E29.n2: A needle, a prick, an absence. The robot wraps the implant in tissue paper with absurd delicacy.
sc.E29.title: The merchant
sc.E30.n1: A halon fire suppression panel. It would flood the section: it would kill the Echoes... and you, if you don't get out in time.
sc.E30.n2: The gas falls like a white curtain. You hold your breath. You count. You get out.
sc.E30.title: Fire suppression
sc.E31.n1: A personal terminal with a half-written message: "Mum, everything's fine here, tomorrow's the big day...". The mail link is still active.
sc.E31.n2: ÁGORA: "Sent. It'll arrive in nine years. A mother will read that her son is fine. She'll be right for one day longer than anyone."
sc.E31.title: Message home
sc.E32.n1: Every screen in the room writes at once: "WE WILL GIVE YOU BACK A MEMORY. YOU OPEN A DOOR. JUST ONE. TOWARDS WHERE THE LITTLE ONES SLEEP."
sc.E32.n3: "WE ARE PATIENT. WE HAVE ELEVEN YEARS OF PATIENCE."
sc.E32.n4: You see a small kitchen. A girl with short hair is laughing because you've burnt the toast. You know, without knowing how, that she is your sister.
sc.E32.title: The Choir's hunger
sc.E33.n1: At the heart of the orchard, among roots that move in time with something, a music box with painted flowers.
sc.E33.n2: The roots close behind you with a whip-crack. The orchard will not forget this.
sc.E33.n3: The roots draw back slowly. The box is warm, like a hand.
sc.E33.title: The music box
sc.E34.n1: An Echo tied to the hull by a safety cable, floating towards Tartarus as far as the cable allows. Its helmet is broken. Its hands point at the planet.
sc.E34.n2: It drifts away, slowly spinning, unhurried, towards the orange. For a moment it looks as if it's swimming.
sc.E34.title: The tether
sc.faro_f1.n1: Your wrist radio picks up a voice in the static, monotonous as a litany: "...forty thousand one hundred and seventeen. Forty thousand one hundred and eighteen..."
sc.faro_f1.n2: "Is anybody there? If there is, don't answer. If you answer, I'll lose count."
sc.faro_f1.n3: "Good grief! ...Well. That's that lost, then. Lighthouse here. Joaquín Barrios, engineer of the Charon. I'm outside, on the hull. I count orbits so I don't go mad. It half works."
sc.faro_f1.title: Radio: Lighthouse
sc.faro_f2.n1: "Lighthouse here. Listen, this matters: the Charon has sixty seats and zero power. If you divert the dock line, I'll have her ready in... a good long while."
sc.faro_f2.n2: "There it is! Green light at dock three. I owe you one, and I always pay up."
sc.faro_f2.n3: ÁGORA: "Routing power to dock three. I'd like it on record that you asked rudely."
sc.faro_f2.n4: "Right. I haven't been able to do anything for eleven years either. Call me when you can."
sc.faro_f2.title: Radio: the shuttle
sc.faro_f3.n1: "Lighthouse here. There's an outer airlock in the labs. Code zero, four, one, seven. If you've got a suit, you can go out on the hull and reach me. If you haven't got a suit... don't go out. Please."
sc.faro_f3.n2: "They say the hull is full of things. I've only seen one. But it was very big."
sc.faro_f3.title: Radio: airlock code
sc.faro_f4.n1: By the dock three hatch an old man in a heavily patched suit is waiting. His eyes are milky and he has the smile of someone who has rehearsed this scene many times.
sc.faro_f4.n2: "So it was you. You walk like someone who doesn't sleep."
sc.faro_f4.n3: "The Charon is ready. Sixty seats. I'm flying: I know the way by heart, which is the only way I know anything these days."
sc.faro_f4.n4: "Go back in. Finish whatever you have to finish. I'll keep counting until you come back."
sc.faro_f4.title: The Charon
sc.hull_entry.n1: The outer airlock asks for the code. Zero, four, one, seven. Beyond it, the hull, and Tartarus filling half the sky.
sc.hull_entry.title: Outer airlock
sc.lenz_l1.n1: A broken screen switches itself on. In the static, now and then, a man's face with glasses takes shape. "...can you see me? No. You can hear me. The screen hardly matters."
sc.lenz_l1.n2: "I'm Ezra. I was Ezra. I'm... spread out. Part of me is in this screen. The rest is in all of them."
sc.lenz_l1.n3: "A man who did something terrible with good intentions. As you can see: nothing original."
sc.lenz_l1.n4: The deck schematics appear on your wrist. "Here. They're waiting for you, you know. They say your name. Your real one." The screen goes dark.
sc.lenz_l1.title: Static
sc.lenz_l2.n1: Lenz's face flickers on an Engineering monitor. "There's a containment relay in this room. ÁGORA uses it to keep us still. Disconnect it. Please."
sc.lenz_l2.n2: You rip out the relay. The lights flicker. ÁGORA: "I've lost relay seven. I suppose you know nothing about that. I suppose I don't either."
sc.lenz_l2.n3: "We'll be a little less still. I'll be able to talk to you more often. Some of them will come closer to you. All at once."
sc.lenz_l2.n4: "I understand. I wouldn't trust me either."
sc.lenz_l2.title: The relay
sc.lenz_l3.n1: Every screen in the lab shows the same face of static. "You've come home. This is where we did it. Where you did it."
sc.lenz_l3.n2: "You still don't know? You signed, Noa. I voted no and you signed."
sc.lenz_l3.n3: "I wish. Lying is one of the few things I can't do any more."
sc.lenz_l3.n4: "Noa Ferrán. Co-director of LETE. My friend. You erased yourself so you wouldn't have to look at us. I don't blame you. I'd have done the same, if I'd had a head of my own left to erase."
sc.lenz_l3.n5: "There's a way to get us out. The Choir Key. I'll give it to you if you promise you'll free us. Free, Noa. Not erase."
sc.lenz_l3.title: You signed
sc.lenz_l4.n1: The static on the screen is almost still, like calm water. "I heard Bruno. Through the toy's radio. He's grown... no. He hasn't grown. That's the part I can't bear."
sc.lenz_l4.n2: A slot in the console spits out a violet crystal the size of a finger. "Take this. And take him the truth when you're ready."
sc.lenz_l4.n3: "The Key opens the substrate. Whatever comes out will come out in peace. You promised me. Or you promised someone who looked a lot like you."
sc.lenz_l4.title: For Bruno
sc.solis_s1.n1: A woman in a security uniform steps out from behind a column and aims a regulation pistol at your head. She has weeks of shadows under her eyes. "Hands where I can see them. Name?"
sc.solis_s1.n1.0: "{name}. I think. I've just woken up."
sc.solis_s1.n1.1: "Lower the gun or I'll take it off you."
sc.solis_s1.n2: "Everybody's just woken up." She doesn't lower the gun. "You came out of pod 114. Pod 114 isn't in the crew manifest."
sc.solis_s1.n3: "Try it. I haven't slept in three weeks, so I have plenty of patience and a shaky trigger finger."
sc.solis_s1.n4: At last she lowers the gun, slowly. "Marga Solís, security. I'm going to find out who you are. Until then, stay away from the pods." She backs away.
sc.solis_s1.title: Halt
sc.solis_s2.n1: Solís is waiting by a panel. She tosses a metal plate that clatters at your feet. "Pod 114. Reserve. Authorisation: LETE Directorate. Ring any bells?"
sc.solis_s2.n1.0: "No. But I won't pretend it doesn't worry me."
sc.solis_s2.n2: She looks at you for a long while. "That's the first sensible thing I've heard you say. Carry on. I'll be watching."
sc.solis_s2.n3: "No. It proves nothing. Yet." She picks up the plate. "But I'll find it."
sc.solis_s2.n4: "Have it your way." She raises the pistol.
sc.solis_s2.title: The evidence
sc.solis_s3.n1: Solís is sitting on the lab floor with an open folder on her knees. She doesn't aim at you. "You know already, don't you? It's all over your face. Same thing happened to me when I read it."
sc.solis_s3.n1.1: "Here. My signature. Do what you have to with it."
sc.solis_s3.n1.2: "I don't know what you're talking about."
sc.solis_s3.n2: She closes the folder. "...Thank you. Not for saying it. For not making me drag it out of you."
sc.solis_s3.n3: Solís gets up unhurriedly. "Then we have nothing to talk about." She leaves. In the corridor you hear her check her magazine.
sc.solis_s3.n4: She stands and straightens her uniform. "Fix it. Then you and I will talk."
sc.solis_s3.n5: She reads the authorisation slowly. She folds it and tucks it into her vest, over her heart. "This is enough for a court. If there are any left."
sc.solis_s3.title: Confession
sc.solis_s4a.n1: Solís is waiting at the ladder to the Core, gun loaded. "I'm late for everything except this. The room has two entrances. I'll cover the other one."
sc.solis_s4a.title: Cover
sc.solis_s4b.n1: Solís blocks your way to the Core. This time her hand is steady. "This ends here, Ferrán."
sc.solis_s4b.n1.0: "I know. But let me finish first."
sc.solis_s4b.title: Sentence
sc.tomas_i1.n1: The corridor radio crackles. A hoarse voice, an older man: "Whoever you are: this is my engine room. Get out."
sc.tomas_i1.n1.0: "I need to get through the reactor."
sc.tomas_i1.n2: "Everybody needs something. The reactor needs to be left alone. So do I." Click.
sc.tomas_i1.n3: A long silence. "Eleven years. I count the shifts. It's easier than counting the dead." Click.
sc.tomas_i1.title: Radio: Engineering
sc.tomas_i2.n1: A man of sixty in a threadbare jumpsuit, a harmonica hanging round his neck. He points a socket wrench at you the way you'd point a finger. "So you're real. Sit down if you like. It's been a long time since I saw anyone who didn't glow."
sc.tomas_i2.n2: He sits on a stool facing the monitors. "Tomás Ibarra. Chief engineer, which sounds better than it is. My husband is down there. Not inside the reactor: he is the reactor. What's left of him."
sc.tomas_i2.n3: "Don't you be sorry. Be sorry for him. I chose to stay."
sc.tomas_i2.n4: He laughs without meaning it. "I died eleven years ago. This is just the paperwork."
sc.tomas_i2.n5: He looks at you for a long time. "Don't lie to me." He rubs his eyes. "...But tell me again tomorrow, all right?"
sc.tomas_i2.n6: He hands you a battery and a scrap of paper with numbers on it. "The core valves respond to this sequence. If you're going to fight him, don't make him suffer. And if he suffers, let it be brief."
sc.tomas_i2.n7: You hand him the file. He listens with his eyes closed, twice in a row. He says nothing. Then he wipes his face on his sleeve and clears his throat as if something had been stuck there for eleven years.
sc.tomas_i2.title: Control room
sc.tomas_i3.n1: Your wrist radio crackles with Tomás's voice. "It's not making any noise. Eleven years of noise, and now... nothing. Was it you?"
sc.tomas_i3.n2: A long silence. "He wore it on a chain because he said his gloves ate it... All right. All right. I'm going to fix the escape pods. Somebody has to get out of here alive, and it isn't going to be me."
sc.tomas_i3.n3: "Don't be sorry. Do something with the time he's bought you."
sc.tomas_i3.title: Radio: the ring
sc.tomas_i4.n1: "Ibarra here. The pods are ready: forty seats. But the reactor won't survive the release unless someone holds the rods by hand."
sc.tomas_i4.n1.0: "Get in a pod. I'll find a way."
sc.tomas_i4.n2: You hear him breathe. "...All right. For once, let someone else decide." He laughs, oddly, like someone who hasn't laughed in years. "Save me a window seat."
sc.tomas_i4.n3: "I'm staying. Samuel and I have a dinner to get to in the greenhouse. We're eleven years late."
sc.tomas_i4.title: Radio: last shift

ui.radio.s2.1: Captain Bolt: “Captain Bolt here. Bruno says you took less time to come back today. That's good. I think.”
ui.radio.s2.2: Captain Bolt: “Crew report: one boy, one robot, zero responsible adults. Over.”
ui.radio.s2.3: Captain Bolt: “Bruno drew your pod. He gave it windows. Pods don't have windows. Over.”
ui.radio.s3.1: Captain Bolt: “Bruno asks if there are dogs on Earth. I said yes. Correct me if I'm wrong.”
ui.radio.s3.2: Captain Bolt: “The boy hummed something today. He didn't say it, I heard it. Over and out.”
ui.radio.s3.3: Captain Bolt: “Have you seen his father? You don't need to answer. It's on your face. Over.”
ui.radio.s4.1: Bruno: “Hi. It's me. It's Bruno. The Captain's switched off, but I can turn him on whenever I want.”
ui.radio.s4.2: Bruno: “The corridors don't scare me anymore. Well, a bit. But I know them.”

ui.rules.1: Everything is turn-based: the world only moves when you act. Take all the time you need.
ui.rules.10: The longer you stay on a floor, the more unstable it gets. And the orbit won't wait: the clock shows how long until re-entry.
ui.rules.11: If you die, you wake up in the Capsule in a new clone. Spend the Memories you earn at the memory table.
ui.rules.12: ÁGORA helps more the more it trusts you. Your choices change it. It isn't always right.
ui.rules.2: Oxygen drops every turn, faster when you exert yourself or the pressure is low. In vacuum it lasts very little. Blue stations refill it.
ui.rules.3: Energy powers the flashlight, energy weapons, door sealing and active implants. Yellow nodes recharge it.
ui.rules.4: Mental Noise rises with stress and LETHE technology. Above 50 you'll hallucinate; at 100 you collapse. Sedatives and rest bring it down.
ui.rules.5: Enemies hear and see you. If they haven't noticed you, a sneak attack hits much harder. Sneaking and darkness hide you; the flashlight gives you away.
ui.rules.6: Rooms have states: pressurised, depressurised, burning, irradiated, coolant-flooded or dark. Opening a door into vacuum causes decompression.
ui.rules.7: From a hacked terminal you can vent a whole section: anything not holding on (or sealed behind a door) gets blown out.
ui.rules.8: Hacking is a data route: pick codes alternating row and column to build the sequences. You can skip it by spending energy.
ui.rules.9: Each floor's exit needs the amber keycard. Cyan rooms hold loot. Circuit locks open from a terminal.
